NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING AND AGENDA
NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS
Tuesday, February 28, 2023
ONE OR MORE SUPERVISORS MAY ATTEND VIA VIDEO AND/OR TELEPHONICALLY 
The Navajo County Board of Supervisors will hold a meeting open to the public on Tuesday, February 28, 2023, in the Supervisors’
Chamber in the Navajo County Governmental Complex, 100 East Code Talkers Drive, Holbrook, Arizona. The Board may vote to
meet in a closed executive session to discuss certain matters and for legal advice on any item as indicated on the following
agenda, pursuant to A.R.S. § 38-431.03(A) (3). 
The Navajo County Board of Supervisors finds that it is in the best interest of the community to conduct this public meeting using
a hybrid method in order to serve the public interest. 
Join Zoom Meeting, click here: https://us06web.zoom.us/j/87692173340?pwd=WDU3WWhlZFcxd1JqN1BzYXI1dUdpZz09 
 
Call In Number: 1-253-215-8782 OR 1-346-248-7799 (You may use either teleconference number)
Meeting ID: 876 9217 3340
Passcode: 271616
Persons with disabilities who need accommodation to attend or participate in the meeting may contact the Clerk of the Board’s
office at (928) 524-4053; at least 48 hours prior to the meeting, so an accommodation can be arranged.
Items on the agenda may be considered out of order at the Chairman’s discretion. A copy of the agenda background material
provided to the Board, except items to be considered in executive session, is available for public inspection at Navajo County
website, www.navajocountyaz.gov
“NOTICE TO PARENTS AND LEGAL GUARDIANS: Parents and legal guardians have the right to consent before Navajo County makes a video
or voice recording of a minor child, pursuant to A.R.S. § 1-602(A)(9). The Navajo County Board of Supervisors regular meetings are recorded and
may be viewed on Navajo County’s website, and social media pages. If you permit your child to attend/participate in a televised Navajo County
Board of Supervisors meeting, a recording will be made, and your child’s picture may be posted on Navajo County’s social media pages. You may
exercise your right not to consent by not allowing your child to attend/participate in the meeting.” 
9:00 a.m. Call To Order: Invocation and Pledge of Allegiance
           
1. CALL TO THE PUBLIC: Individuals may address the Board on any relevant issue for up to
3 minutes. At the close of the call to the public, Board members may not respond to any
comments but may respond to criticism, ask staff to review a matter or ask that a matter be
placed on a future agenda.
 
 
2. CONSENT AGENDA: These items are considered to be routine or administrative in nature
and will be approved in a single motion. A Board member may request for any item to be
removed from the consent agenda and considered on the regular agenda:
 
 
a. Minutes: January 24, 2023, Regular Meeting and February 7, 2023, Special Meeting, Regular
and Executive Session
 
 
b. Warrant & Voucher Report over $1000, January 2023  
 
c. Clerk of Superior Court Report: January 2023

<!-- page 2 -->
d. Constable Reports: Holbrook Precinct #1, October-November 2022; Winslow Precinct #2,
September-November 2022, December 2022, January 2023;  Snowflake Precinct #3, January
2023; Show Low Precinct #5, January 2023; Pinetop-Lakeside Precinct #6, January 2023
 
 
e. Justice Court Reports: Holbrook Precinct #1,  Winslow Precinct #2, Snowflake Precinct #3,
Kayenta Precinct #4, Show Low Precinct #5, Pinetop-Lakeside Precinct #6, January 2023
 
 
f. Sympathy Letters: Ryan Taylor (GIS/NCIS), Pam Searls (Superior Court), Robert Riege
(Kirsten Riege Human Resources), Ron Chisholm (Sheriff)
 
 
g. Amendment authorizing the transfer of budget appropriations to the department in which the
expenditure will be recorded
 
 
h. Reissuance of Stale Dated Checks  
 
i. Contracts signed by County Manager/Assistant County Manager pursuant to Board of
Supervisors Resolution: Contract with SGR for recruitment of an Economic Development
Director position for Real AZ  
 
 
j. Resolution Number 03-2023 cancelling the elections on March 14, 2023, for White
Mountain Lakes Special Road District and Timberland Acres Special Road District and
appointing the candidate(s) or deeming the position vacant
 
 
k. A request from Holbrook High School Choir for $1575.00 in ARRF funds from the County
Attorney to help provide for a choir program trip to Disneyland
 
 
l. Amendment Number 4 to the Slurry Seal Contract #B19-01-007 extending the contract one
(1) additional year and increasing the rate for the Winslow area to 1.61 per square yard and
the Show Low, Pinetop-Lakeside area to 1.51 per square yard
 
 
m. Amendment Number 3 extending Employee Benefits Consultant Contract No. B20-01-007
with The Mahoney Group for one additional year from April 1, 2023, through March 31, 2024
 
 
n. Contract Amendment Number 1 extending the Navajo County Jail Medical and Psychological
Services contract with Wexford Health Sources, Inc. for one additional year (March 8, 2023,
through March 7, 2024) was revised to include the staffing chart
 
 
o. Fiscal Year 22/23 Fund Transfers  
 
p. Approval of all properties sold as auctioned on the back tax land on-line auction and approval
to allow the Clerk of the Board to sell the unsold properties over the counter for the amount
due
 
 
q. Appointment of Lucinda Ann Honani, Jolanda Joyce Aguilar and Lydia A. Dosela as

<!-- page 3 -->
q. Appointment of Lucinda Ann Honani, Jolanda Joyce Aguilar and Lydia A. Dosela as
Democratic Precinct Committeemen for their respective precincts
 
 
r. Appointment of Wyatt Edward Buschschulte and Steven Allen Le Sueur as Republican
Precinct Committeemen for their respective precincts
 
 
s. Re-appointment of Chuck Howe and Ruth Ann Smith to four-year term to the Navajo County
Planning and Zoning Commission and appointment of Vance Muder to a four-year term to
the Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission
 
 
t. Amendment Number 1 to the Supplying & Delivering Liquid Asphalt Products, Contract #
B22-01-010 extending the contract one (1) additional year and increasing the rates
 
 
3. NAVAJO COUNTY PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICES DISTRICT: Board of Directors
Session: 
 
 
a. CONSENT AGENDA: The following item(s) are considered to be of a routine or
administrative in nature and will be approved as a group unless a member of the Board
wishes to discuss a particular item: 
 
 
1. Intergovernmental Agreement Amendment Number 2, Contract Number CTR061423
COVID-19 Expansion Project, to extend services through July 31, 2024
 
 
2. Intergovernmental Agreement Amendment Number 1, Contract Number CTR055993 for
COVID19 Health Disparities, contract is hereby extended through May 30, 2024
 
 
3. Intergovernmental Agreement Amendment Number 2, Contract Number CTR057424 for
COVID-19 ELC Funding for K-12 Schools Reopening, to extend services through July 31,
2023
 
 
4. BOARD OF SUPERVISORS:  
 
a. Presentation to Chairwoman Dawnafe Whitesinger for her 2022 service.  
Presented By: Board of Supervisors
 
b. Consideration and appointment of Ashley Dodds, James Derek Scoble, Jason Giangiuli,
Kathy Henderson-Essel, and Scott Hurst to the White Mountain Lakes County Recreation
Improvement District Board of Directors pursuant to the passing of HB2067.
 
Presented By: Melissa Buckley

<!-- page 4 -->
5. EMPLOYEE RECOGNITION:  
 
a. Navajo County recognizes the following employees for their excellence in personal
performance far exceeding organization expectations for the month of February Bryan
Cook (Public Works) and William (Bill) Ricci (Health Department)
 
Presented By: Lea Petersen
 
6. ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES:  
 
a. Personnel Service Awards: Congratulations to the following employees for their continued
service to Navajo County: Joshua Reizer (Sheriff) 5; Erin Johnson (County Attorney) 5; 
Hailee Farkas (Sheriff) 5; Claudette Lester (Jail) 5; Laurie Velde (Assessor) 10; Ron
Smith (Superior Court) 10; Kirby Coppedge (Sheriff) 10; and Latanya Bakurza (County
Attorney) 20.
 
Presented By: Eric Scott
 
b. Presentation to Marc Russell on his Retirement from Navajo County after 18+ years of
service.
 
Presented By: Eric Scott and Deanne Romo
 
c. Presentation to the Navajo County Finance Team for receiving the Certificate of
Achievement for Excellence in Financial Reporting.
 
Presented By: Bryan Layton
 
d. Consideration of approval of Contract with eX2 Technology, LLC (eX2) for the Design,
Construction, Maintenance and Marketing of Fiber Optic Infrastructure and to authorize
change order authority to the County Manager for 2.5% of the System Price amount and
authorize the County Manager to execute the necessary documents.
 
Presented By: Grant Evans
 
7. COUNTY ATTORNEY:  
 
a. Consideration and possible approval of Navajo County's participation in the settlement
agreement reached in the multi-state opioid litigation case with Teva, Allegan, CVS,
Walgreens and Wal-Mart. 
 
Presented By: Jason Moore
 
8. PUBLIC WORKS:  
 
a. Consideration of the purchase of a 2022 CV515 SFA (3 Yard Dump Truck) from RWC
Group in the amount of $127,332.00.
 
Presented By: Madhav Mundle

<!-- page 5 -->
b. PLANNING & ZONNING:  
 
1. PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration and adoption of Resolution Number 04-2023,
approving/denying text amendment to Article 25 of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance
regarding the prohibition against placement/movement of mobile homes 20 years old or
older. 
 
Presented By: Sondra Starke
 
2. PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration of the adoption of Resolution Number 05-2023 
approving/denying a text amendment to Article IX, Navajo County Subdivision Regulations
and Addition of Section 9.4 - Exceptions; Plat Alterations.
 
Presented By: Berrin Nejad
 
3. PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration of the adoption of Resolution Number 06-2023
approving/denying a Zone Change request by Michael James Barclay for the southern
portion of a 10-acre parcel from R1-10 (Single-Family Residential Zoning) to C-R
(Commercial-Residential) to be consistent with the northern portion which is C-R for the
first 300 from northern boundary, White Mountain Lake Road.
 
Presented By: Berrin Nejad
 
4. PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration of the adoption of Resolution Number 07-2023 
approving/denying a Zone Change of a 0.87-acre parcel from A-General (General Zoning
District) to C-R (Commercial-Residential) to build an accounting and tax office. 
 
Presented By: Berrin Nejad
 
5. PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration of the adoption of Resolution Number 08-2023 
approving/denying a Special Use Permit to operate a recovery residential facility for ten
(10) residents with 13 staff per week with overlapping shifts.
 
Presented By: Berrin Nejad
 
c. NAVAJO COUNTY FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT: Board of Directors Session:  
 
1. CONSENT AGENDA: The following item(s) are considered to be of a routine or
administrative in nature and will be approved as a group unless a member of the Board
wishes to discuss a particular item: 
 
 
a. Professional Services Contract with the Tomhave Group, Inc.  
 
9. NORTHEASTERN ARIZONA INNOVATIVE WORKFORCE SOLUTIONS:  
 
a. EXECUTIVE SESSION pursuant to A.R.S. §38-3403.03(A)(3) for the Board to receive
legal advice from its attorney regarding possible action regarding the Local Workforce
Development Board (LWDB) decision to terminate its relationship with the Northeastern
Arizona Community Resources Network (NACRN).
 
Presented By: Jason Moore/Bryan Layton

<!-- page 6 -->
b. EXECUTIVE SESSION pursuant to A.R.S. §38-431.03(A)(3) for the Board to receive
legal advice from its attorney regarding review, consideration and possible action
concerning Keith Sobraske Investigative Report concerning WIOA program and former
Director.
 
Presented By: Jason Moore/Bryan Layton
 
c. RECONVENE: Consideration and possible action regarding the Local Workforce
Development Board (LWDB) decision to terminate its relationship with the Northeastern
Arizona Community Resources Network (NACRN).
 
Presented By: Jason Moore
 
d. RECONVENE: Consideration and possible action concerning Keith Sobraske Investigative
Report concerning WIOA program and former Director.
 
Presented By: Jason Moore
 
10. COUNTY BUSINESS UPDATE: Report from County Manager, County Attorney and
Board members.
 
 
 
11. ADJOURN  
 
Dated: February 24, 2023 NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS 
Posted: 3:30 p.m. By:- MWB
Melissa W. Buckley - Clerk of the Board

Board of Supervisors Regular 2. g.        
Meeting Date: 02/28/2023  
Title: Budget amendment authorizing transfer of budget appropriations.
Submitted By: Jayson Vowell, Finance Director
Department: Administrative Services Division: Finance
Motion before the Board:
Amendment authorizing the transfer of budget appropriations to the department in which the
expenditure will be recorded
Background:
Expenditures may not exceed appropriations at the department level.  In certain instances,
transfers of appropriations between departments or from the contingency account to a
department may be made upon the Board of Supervisor's approval.  Due to the timing of the
approval of the Fiscal Year 2022-2023 budget, the compensation/market adjustments were
appropriated in different departments (department 019 for the general fund and department 002
for the special revenue funds).  This transfer allocates the budget appropriation to the applicable
department in which the expenditure will be recorded.
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: 2023
Budgeted Y/N: Y
Amount Requested: $0
Fiscal Impact:
None.

Board of Supervisors Regular 2. h.        
Meeting Date: 02/28/2023  
Title: Reissuance of Stale Dated Checks
Submitted For: Kari Lopez, Treasurer  Submitted By: Olivia Todd, Chief Deputy
Treasurer
Department: Treasurer
Motion before the Board:
Reissuance of Stale Dated Checks
Background:
Treasurer's checks were issued as refunds for overpaid property taxes or for investor payments.
The checks were voided because they had been outstanding for a year or more. The payees
were contacted and are requesting replacement checks. All have completed the required
Affidavit For Issuance of Duplicate Warrant form. Upon approval, a new check will be issued to
the individuals pursuant to A.R.S. §11-632.

Board of Supervisors Regular 2. j.        
Meeting Date: 02/28/2023  
Title: C&A Special Road Dist. Election for March 14 2023
Submitted By: Rayleen Richards, Elections Director
Department: Elections
Motion before the Board:
Resolution Number 03-2023 cancelling the elections on March 14, 2023, for White Mountain
Lakes Special Road District and Timberland Acres Special Road District and appointing the
candidate(s) or deeming the position vacant
Background:
48-1404. Election of trustees; vacancies
B. The election shall be held at such places as the board of trustees shall by resolution
determine, after notice thereof posted for ten days next preceding the election in three
conspicuous places in each precinct into which the district may be divided for the purposes of
election.  Candidates for the office of trustee shall file nominating petitions with the board of
supervisors as prescribed by title 16, chapter 3.  If only one person files or no person files a
nominating petition for an election to fill a district office, the board of supervisors may cancel
the election for the position and appoint the person who filed the nominating petition to fill the
position. If no person files a nominating petition for an election to fill a district office, the board
of supervisors may cancel the election for that office and that office is deemed vacant and shall
be filled as otherwise provided by law.  A person who is appointed pursuant to this section is
fully vested with the powers and duties of the office as if elected to that office.

RESOLUTION NO ______ - 23 
 
A RESOLUTION OF THE NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS, CANCELLING THE ELECTIONS FOR 
WHITE MOUNTAIN LAKE SPECIAL ROAD DISTRICT #2 AND TIMBELAND ACRES SPECIAL ROAD DISTRICT; 
AND APPOINTING THE CANDIDATE(S) or DEEMING POSITION(S) VACANT, PURSUANT TO ARS § 48-1404 
(B) 
 
 
WHEREAS, ARS § 48-1404 (B) provides as follows with respect to Special Road District Board of Directors 
positions: 
 
              “If only one person files or no person files a nominating petition for an election to fill a district office, 
the board of supervisors may cancel the election for the position and appoint the person who filed the 
nominating petition to fill the position. If no person files a nominating petition for an election to fill a district 
office, the board of supervisors may cancel the election for that office and that office is deemed vacant and 
shall be filled as otherwise provided by law.  A person who is appointed pursuant to this section is fully vested 
with the powers and duties of the office as if elected to that office.” 
 
         and 
 
WHEREAS, A.R.S. § 16-410 (A) authorizes the Board to take such action no earlier than one hundred and 
five (105) days before the election, and it is now less than one hundred and five (105) days before the March 14, 
2023 Special Election at which the Special Road District Board of Directors will be elected; 
 
         and 
 
WHEREAS, the officer in charge of elections, has certified that the number of persons who filed nominating 
petitions to fill the Special Road District Board of Directors positions is less than or equal to the number of positions 
available, attached hereto and incorporated herein as “Exhibit A”;

<!-- page 485 -->
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Supervisors as follows:  
 
 
That the Special Road District Board of Directors position(s), attached hereto and incorporated herein as 
“Exhibit A”, are hereby deemed Elected or positions deemed vacant by the Navajo County Board of Supervisors. 
 
 
 
          PASSED, APPROVED AND ADOPTED at Holbrook, Arizona on Feb. 28, 2023

Attorney to help provide for a choir program trip to Disneyland
Background:
The Holbrook High School Choir has an opportunity for students to participate in a trip that will
be a positive experience which helps to prevent gang involvement and substance abuse.  The trip
will serve as a development and positive engagement, giving students opportunities to build
relationships and develop teamwork and leadership skills.  Being surrounded by peers who share
the same interests and goals can be a factor against gang involvement and substance abuse.

Board of Supervisors Regular 2. l.        
Meeting Date: 02/28/2023  
Title: Amendment No. 4 to Slurry Seal Contract #B19-01-007 Districts 1, 4 & 5
Submitted For: Madhav Mundle, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Stevie Studer, Account Specialist
Department: Public Works
Motion before the Board:
Amendment Number 4 to the Slurry Seal Contract #B19-01-007 extending the contract one (1)
additional year and increasing the rate for the Winslow area to 1.61 per square yard and the
Show Low, Pinetop-Lakeside area to 1.51 per square yard
Background:
Navajo County Public Works maintains approximately 730 miles of roads throughout the
County, of which approximately 330 miles are paved.  Application of a slurry seal on asphalt
roads extends the life of the pavement.  On February 26, 2019, the Board of Supervisors
approved the contract with American Pavement Preservation, LLC for Slurry Seal Contract
#B19-01-007. This contract has worked very well for Navajo County and upon written mutual
agreement, Navajo County may renew the contract for up to four (4) additional one-year terms.
This would be the fourth renewal and concurrence has been received by the contractor with an
increase for the Winslow area to 1.61 per square yard and the Show Low, Pinetop-Lakeside area
to 1.51 per square yard. This is an overall increase of 0.161 per square yard for all areas, which
is due to the increase in the rising cost of emulsion based materials only. No other factors were
calculated into the requested increase. This contract does allow for an increase in the event
economic conditions are such that price increases become necessary. The vendor has submitted
to the Public Works Department a formal request for the increase and has provided supporting
documentation. Staff has reviewed the request and recommends approval.
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: 2023&2024
Budgeted Y/N: Y
Amount Requested:
Fiscal Impact:
Funds are budgeted under capital outlay for FY 2023 & 2024.

Board of Supervisors Regular 2. q.        
Meeting Date: 02/28/2023  
Title: PC DEM Appointment
Submitted By: Rayleen Richards, Elections Director
Department: Elections
Motion before the Board:
Appointment of Lucinda Ann Honani, Jolanda Joyce Aguilar and Lydia A. Dosela as
Democratic Precinct Committeemen for their respective precincts
Background:
Appointment valid through Oct. 1, 2024.
16-821. County committee; vacancy in office of precinct committeeman
B. The board of supervisors upon the recommendation of the county chairman, or the
recommendation of a committee designated in the bylaws of the county committee for that
purpose, shall determine when a vacancy exists in the office of precinct committeeman. If a
vacancy exists, the vacancy shall be filled by the board of supervisors from a list of names
submitted by the county chairman of the appropriate political party. Only a precinct
committeeman elected at the primary election prior to the date of a state or county committee
organizing meeting shall be permitted to vote at such meeting. The criteria used to establish
when a vacancy exists in the office of precinct committeeman shall be as established in section
38-291.
 
 
 16-822. Precinct committeemen; eligibility; vacancy; duties; term
  
Any member of a recognized political party who is a registered voter in the precinct is
eligible to seek the office of precinct committeeman of that party in that precinct.
A.
F. The term of office of a precinct committeeman is two years and begins on October 1 after the
primary election at which the precinct committeeman was a candidate and continues until
October 1 after the following primary election at which a precinct committeeman is elected.

Planning and Zoning Commission and appointment of Vance Muder to a four-year term to the
Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission
Background:
The Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission advises and makes recommendations to
the Board of Supervisors on matters of planning, zoning, and subdivision planning.  Typical
issues considered by the Commission include rezoning request, Special Use Permis, and Zoning
Ordinance amendments. Currently, there are vacancies due to term expirations in District I, III
and IV.

Board of Supervisors Regular 2. t.        
Meeting Date: 02/28/2023  
Title: Amendment No. 1 to Supplying & Delivering Liquid Asphalt Products, Contract #
B22-01-010
Submitted For: Madhav Mundle, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Jeanine Carruthers, Deputy Director Administration
Department: Public Works
Motion before the Board:
Amendment Number 1 to the Supplying & Delivering Liquid Asphalt Products, Contract #
B22-01-010 extending the contract one (1) additional year and increasing the rates
Background:
This is an annual contract to provide the sale and delivery (as required), application, and other
aspects of liquid asphalt products used for the County's pavement preservation work in patching
potholes, chip seal application and fog seal treatments on public roads in Navajo County.  On
March 8, 2022, the Board of Supervisors approved the contract with Hawker & Evan Asphalt
Co., Inc. Contract # B22-01-010 Supplying & Delivering Liquid Asphalt Products.  This
contract has worked very well for Navajo County and upon mutual agreement, Navajo County
may renew the contract up to four (4) additional one-year terms.  This would be the first
renewal and concurrence has been received by the contractor.  The asphalt  industry has
received extreme increases in emulsifiers, polymer, kerosene, labor costs, equipment
operational costs, and general inflationary costs, which have been factored into the price
increase.  Staff has reviewed the request and recommends approval.

Title: Contract No. CTR061423 Amendment 2
Submitted By: Rochelle Spencer, Deputy Health Director
Department: NC Public Health Services District
Motion before the Board:
Intergovernmental Agreement Amendment Number 2, Contract Number CTR061423
COVID-19 Expansion Project, to extend services through July 31, 2024
Background:
This contract allows capability to enhance our disease surveillance and epidemiological
capabilities for more comprehensive and robust response to circulating infectious disease and
outbreaks.  This amendment extends the funding deadline, allowing us to expend any remaining
funds on activities pertaining to the following goals: 
Goal 1: Leverage and build upon existing public health infrastructure that emphasizes the
coordination and critical integration of    disease investigation, epidemiology, contact
tracing, and maximize the public health impact of availability.
Goal 2: Reduce transmission of diseases to students, teachers, and staff in schools, which
will help prevent infection in the w community;
Goal 3: Continue to advocate for increased access to reliable testing with quick
turn-around time for results, efficient case findings and contact tracing, reduce barriers to
improve access to testing and ensure free/affordable testing options are available
throughout the community; and
Goal 4: Continue and enhance existing community outreach, communication, education
and networking activities related to COVID-19.

Board of Supervisors Regular 4. b.        
Meeting Date: 02/28/2023  
Title: Appointment of Board of Directors WMLCRID
Submitted By: Melissa Buckley, Clerk of the Board of Supervisors
Department: Board of Supervisors
Presented By: Melissa Buckley
Motion before the Board:
Consideration and appointment of Ashley Dodds, James Derek Scoble, Jason Giangiuli, Kathy
Henderson-Essel, and Scott Hurst to the White Mountain Lakes County Recreation
Improvement District Board of Directors pursuant to the passing of HB2067.
Background:
On November 8, 2022, the Board of Supervisors adopted Resolution Number 36, 2022,
approving the establishment of a separate governance structure for the White Mountain Lakes
County Recreation Improvement District, governed by a five (5) member board. 
We received thirteen (13) applications for the five (5) member board. All applications were
verified and twelve (12) of the applicants met the requirements to sit on the Board of Directors.
One (1) applicant was not registered to vote in Navajo County and therefore was disqualified.
Each of the twelve (12) applicants underwent a background check. 
The Board of Supervisors along with the Clerk of the Board reviewed the applications,
verification and background checks and submitted their top five (5) applicants. 
  
Name TOTAL
Ashley Dodds 5
James Derek Scoble 4
Jason Giangiuli 5
Kathy Henderson-Essel 4
Scott Hurst 4
Upon appointment Navajo County staff will coordinate with the WMLCRID Board of Directors
to schedule an initial training during their first Board of Directors meeting. 
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends appointment of the 5 applicants to make up the Board of Directors for the
White Mountain Lakes County Recreation Improvement District.

Board of Supervisors Regular 6. c.        
Meeting Date: 02/28/2023  
Title: CAFR Award to Navajo County Finance
Submitted By: Leah Thomas, Deputy Clerk of the Board of Supervisors
Department: Administrative Services
Presented By: Bryan Layton
Subject:
Presentation to the Navajo County Finance Team for receiving the Certificate of Achievement
for Excellence in Financial Reporting.
Background: 
The Navajo County Finance team has received the Certificate of Achievement for Excellence in
Financial Reporting by the Government Finance Officers Association of the United States and
Canada (GFOA) for its comprehensive annual financial report. Navajo County’s annual
financial report was judged by an impartial panel to meet the high standards of the program,
which includes demonstrating a constructive “spirit of full disclosure” to clearly communicate
its financial story.  This is the eleventh consecutive year that the County has received this
prestigious award.  The GFOA established the Certificate of Achievement for Excellence in
Financial Reporting Program (Certificate Program) in 1945 to encourage and assist state and
local governments to go beyond the minimum requirements of generally accepted accounting
principles to prepare annual comprehensive reports that evidence the spirit of transparency and
full disclosure and then to recognize individual governments that succeed in achieving that
goal.  The Certificate of Achievement is the highest form of recognition in the area of
governmental accounting and financial reporting, and its attainment represents a significant
accomplishment by Navajo County and the Finance Team.

Board of Supervisors Regular 6. d.        
Meeting Date: 02/28/2023  
Title: Contract for the Design, Construction, Maintenance and Marketing of Fiber Optic
Infrastructure
Submitted For: Grant Evans, Capital Projects Manager 
Submitted By: Grant Evans, Capital Projects Manager
Department: Public Works
Presented By: Grant Evans
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of approval of Contract with eX2 Technology, LLC (eX2) for the Design,
Construction, Maintenance and Marketing of Fiber Optic Infrastructure and to authorize change
order authority to the County Manager for 2.5% of the System Price amount and authorize the
County Manager to execute the necessary documents.
Background:
On January 26, 2021, Navajo County hired Magellan Advisors to develop a broadband
infrastructure Strategic Plan. On December 14, 2021, the BOS approved said Strategic Plan
which identified construction of an open-access middle mile network as a first priority for the
County to invest in.  Through adoption of Resolution Number 36-21 also on December 14,
2021, the BOS supported the build of this identified middle mile project and authorized a
request for proposal (RFP) to seek private sector partners to be included in a future grant
submittal to the Arizona Commerce Authority (ACA) for the purpose of completing this
project. Then, on January 25, 2022, the BOS approved the funding package for the County
ARPA projects, including ten million dollars for broadband.  It was on this date that the BOS
also approved the selection of WANRack, LLC as the Evaluation Committee’s highest-ranking
firm for Fiber Optic Network Provider, RFP #B21-11-030. Also, on January 25, 2022, through
adoption of Resolution Number 01-22, the BOS supported a grant submittal to the Arizona
Commerce Authority (ACA) for the purpose of completing the middle mile broadband network
including a financial contribution of up to nine million dollars as local match funds.  In July of
2022, the County was awarded an ACA grant in the amount of $9,734,083.06.  After WANRack
and the County were unable to come together on the terms and conditions of an Agreement to
move the project forward, on September 13, 2022, the BOS approved a change in our Fiber
Optic Network Provider, #B21-11-030 for Navajo County to eX2, in accordance with the
Arizona Commerce Authority Broadband Development Grant awarded July 2022.  Since that
date, staff has worked with eX2 negotiating this important agreement.
While the grant funds from the ACA have not yet been received, the provisions of this contract
allow the County to cautiously move the project forward. As the US Treasury reviews the ACA
grant application, eX2 can start the project design.  We would expect that the grant funds will
be released prior to the design being completed.  By expediting the design phase, the County

<!-- page 565 -->
will be able to bring broadband availability to our residents in a timelier manner.
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends approval of the Contract with eX2 and to authorize change order authority to
the County Manager for 2.5% of the System Price amount (as shown in Schedule 3.1) and
authorize the County Manager to execute the necessary documents.
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: 23/24/25
Budgeted Y/N: Partial
Amount Requested: 20,271,814
Fiscal Impact:
The total amount requested is $20,271,813.59. This project is Partially Funded Pending ACA
Grant Receipt. The funding for this project includes $9,734,083.06 from the ACA ADBG
grant and $10,000,000 from ARPA funds.  $494,434.48 would be a reserve fund for project
changes.  The ACA ADBG grant funds are pending receipt from the grantor.

CONTRACT FOR THE DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, MAINTENANCE AND 
MARKETING OF FIBER OPTIC INFRASTRUCTURE 
 
 This Contract for the Design, Construction, Maintenance and Marketing of Fiber Optic  
Infrastructure ("Contract") is made and entered into this 1st day of March, 2023 ("Effective Date") 
by and between Navajo County, Arizona, a political subdivision of the State of Arizona with a 
place of business at 100 E. Code Talkers Drive , Holbrook, Arizona 86025 ("County"), and eX2 
Technology, LLC, a Nebraska limited liability company with a place of business at 1044 N. 115th 
Street, Suite 200, Omaha, Nebraska 68154 ("Contractor"). 
  
 WHEREAS, County wants to procure all materials and services for the design, 
construction, maintenance and marketing of new fiber optic infrastructure to be installed along 
County, other public, and private right-of-way (the "ROW); 
 
 WHEREAS, County issued a Request for Proposal – Fiber Optic Network Provider, and 
in response, Contractor submitted a Proposal on January 10, 2022 as supplemented on October 28, 
2022  (collectively, the "Proposal"); and 
 
 WHEREAS, in reliance on the Proposal and based on a comparison of County's needs and 
the proposals offered by all respondents, County determined that Contractor possesses the best 
overall technical capability, project management, marketing knowledge, financial strength and 
experience required to design, construct, maintain and market County's fiber optic infrastructure. 
 
 NOW THEREFORE , in consideration of the premises and mutual promises and 
covenants contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and 
sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties hereby agree as follows: 
 
ARTICLE 1 
THE PROJECT; TERM 
 
 1.1 The Project.  County hereby retains Contractor to (i) design, construct and maintain  
a new multi-conduit fiber optic system (the "Fiber Optic System") along County ROW and other 
public and private right -of-way (the " Non-County ROW"), and (ii) exclusively market certain 
portions of the System to third parties, all as described in more detail in the terms and conditions 
set forth in this Contract, its Schedules and Exhibits (collectively, the "Project").  The Fiber Optic 
System shall sometimes hereinafter be referred to as the "System". 
 
 1.2 Term.  Unless earlier terminated as described elsewhere in this Contract, t he term 
shall expire ten (10) years following the System Acceptance Date (the "Term").  The Term shall 
automatically renew for two (2) successive five (5) year periods, unless either party provides a 
written non-renewal notice to the other party at least one hundred eighty (180) days prior to the 
expiration of the then-current Term.  Notwithstanding the foregoing, any renewal of the Term shall 
be subject to (i) the continued validity of underlying right-of-way for the System, recognizing that 
any additional Costs incurred by Contractor for extensions of right-of-way beyond the initial Term 
shall be passed through to County, and (ii) the continued operability of the System (e.g., fiber 
degradation), which shall be determined in Contractor's reasonable discretion  after consultation 
with County. 
 
 1.3 Defined Terms.  As used in this Contract, capitalized terms shall have the meanings 
specified in Schedule 1.3, Defined Terms, and in any other Schedule , Exhibit or in the body of 
this Contract.

ARTICLE 2 
SCOPE OF WORK;  SITE ACCESS 
 
 2.1 Scope of Work.  The work under this Contract shall be performed for the County 
on a segment-by-segment basis, both within the County ROW and the Non-County ROW.  The 
implementation schedule, a description of the segments (each, a " Segment") that comprise the 
System and a description of the scope of work ("Scope of Work") to be performed are set forth in 
the attached Schedule 2.1, Scope of Work.   
 
 2.2 Site Conditions. 
 
 2.2.1 Inspection.  Contractor has inspected the installation sites and is familiar 
with the conditions of the sites.  In the event Contractor encounters toxic or hazardous 
materials in the performance of this Contract, which toxic or hazardous materials were not 
introduced to the site by Contractor, Contractor shall not be required to proceed with the 
Project until County or the appropriate Government Authority, organization or party has 
removed such toxic or hazardous materials and/or otherwise remediated the affected 
installation site, and any resulting delays shall be considered a force majeure  event in 
accordance with Section 14.4, Force Majeure.  Furthermore, Contractor shall prepare and 
deliver to County prior to bringing any hazardous materials onto the County ROW a list of 
any such hazardous materials.   
 
 2.2.2 Concealed Conditions.   Contractor acknowledges that concealed 
conditions that may affect the cost of Contractor's performance of this Contract may exist.  
Contractor shall promptly, and before such conditions ar e disturbed, notify County in 
writing of any: (a) subsurface or latent physical conditions at the installation sites differing 
materially from those indicated in this Contract or the attached Schedules and Exhibits; or 
(b) unknown physical conditions at the site, of an unusual nature, differing materially from 
those ordinarily encountered and generally recognized as inherent in the work of the 
character provided for in this Contract.  County shall promptly investigate the conditions, 
and if it finds that su ch conditions exist and that they are likely to cause a significant 
increase or decrease in the time and/or expense required for completion of a Segment, then 
County and Contractor shall negotiate in good faith toward an equitable adjustment of the 
time and expense required for such completion. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Contractor 
shall under no circumstances be responsible for additional costs for any conditions that 
County has knowledge of as of the date of execution hereof, or any archeological finds, 
antiquities or County-placed items not disclosed to Contractor prior to the Effective Date. 
 
 2.3 Delivery and Transportation.  Contractor shall cause the Materials to be delivered 
in accordance with the delivery dates specified in the Progress Schedule to either, at the reasonable 
discretion of County, County-designated locations at the sites or storage or staging areas.  County 
agrees to cooperate with Contractor as is reasonably necessary to identify storage or staging areas 
in reasonable proximity to the installation sites.  Contractor shall arrange for all transportation of 
the Materials to County-designated locations at the sites and shall be responsible for making proper 
arrangements with the necessary officials for the use of any public roads and streets for hauling 
loads in excess of present permitted allowances.  When Contractor is allowed to use County ROW 
for storage of Materials, stockpiles shall be confined to such cleared areas as may be approved by 
County.  The use of such storage sites on County ROW shall be discontinued immediately upon 
completion of that portion of the Project for which the storage was required and the sites shall be

cleaned of all surplus materials and debris introduced to the site by Contractor or its Subcontractors 
and restored substantially to their original condition by Contractor at its sole cost and expense. 
 
 2.4 Access to County ROW.  As of the Effective Date, County grants to Contractor, 
and Contractor hereby accepts from County, at no cost or expense to Contractor, an exclusive 
license to access the County ROW to perform all Construction Services and Maintenance Services 
on the System during the Term in accordance with the terms of this Contract (the "County ROW 
License").  For clarity, the parties recognize that Contractor shall obtain individual construction 
permits to perform the Construction Services and Maintenance Services within the County ROW 
pursuant to the County ROW License, at no additional cost or expense to Contractor, as further 
described in Section 13.1, Permits and Licenses.   
 
 2.5 Access to Non -County ROW.  As of the Effective Date , County agrees to use 
commercially reasonable efforts to assist Contractor in obtaining any permits and licenses that are 
required to perform the Services hereunder on Non-County ROW.  
 
 2.6 Title; Risk of Loss.  Title and all risk of loss or damage to the Materials shall remain 
vested in and upon Contractor until a Segment of the System has achieved Segment Acceptance 
as provided in Section 6.2.2(c), Segment Acceptance  Upon Segment Acceptance and payment 
in full, legal title and risk of loss or damage to the Materials for such Segment shall pass to County.

3.2 Marketing; Revenue. 
 
 3.2.1 Contractor Marketing.  County hereby appoints Contractor as its exclusive 
marketing agent with respect to marketing and promoting the use of the System by System 
Users, as further described herein.  Such appointment shall be coterminous with the Term 
of this Contract, unless otherwise  terminated in accordance with the terms of Article 11, 
Default, Remedies and Termination .  Contractor shall undertake to identify potential 
System Users and otherwise market and promote the System to maximize System use.  For 
clarity, the parties recogniz e that Contractor shall not market that portion of the System

County's internal use, as further described in Section 3.2.4, County Duct and Fiber .  
Contractor shall negotiate with potential System Users on County's behalf in connection 
with such System Users entering into user agreements in substantially the forms set forth 
in Exhibit 1, Form of User Agreement:  Dark Fiber IRU Agreement  ("User 
Agreement") that will govern the use of the System by such System Users.  Contractor 
shall coordinate with County with respect to the negotiation of pricing and other terms and

County for its final approval and execution.  County may accept or reject any User 
Agreements tendered by Contractor in County's reasonable discretion; provided that 
County shall not reject a User Agreement if such User Agreement is tendered to County in 
a form substantially similar to the forms set forth in Exhibit 1, Form of User Agreement:  
Dark Fiber IRU Agreement and contains pricing terms reasonably acceptable to County.  
All of the foregoing marketing and promotional services described in this Section 3.2 are 
collectively referred to as "Marketing Services."

 3.2.2 Non-Discrimination.  Contractor agrees that it shall market and promote 
the rights in, through and to the System to third parties in a non -discriminatory and  
competitively neutral manner.  
 
 3.2.3 Revenue Sharing.   County and Contractor will share the revenues 
generated by Contractor's marketing and promotion of the System , as described in 
Schedule 3.2.3, Sharing of System Revenues.  Contractor shall pay County, within thirty 
(30) days, County's share of the System Revenues paid by System Users.  In the event

to the continuing performance of the applicable System User, Contractor shall be entitled 
to its share of System Revenues generated during the entire term of such User Agreements, 
regardless of whether this Contract expires or is terminated for any reason during the term 
of any such User Agreement.   
 
 3.2.4 County Duct and Fiber; Limitations Upon Use .   County retains the sole 
and exclusive right to use the County Duct and the County Fibers.  County shall not license, 
lease, sell or provide any other rights in, through and to County Duct(s) and/or County 
Fibers to any third party.   
 
   3.2.5 Marketing Plan.  Within sixty (60) calendar days of the System Acceptance 
Date, unless otherwise noted, Contractor shall develop and submit to County a marketing 
plan (the "Marketing Plan") reasonably designed to accomplish the goals described in this 
Section 3.2, Marketing; Revenue.   
 
 3.2.6 Marketing Reports.  Contractor shall submit to County, upon request but 
no more frequently than quarterly, a progress report of the marketing activities during the 
reporting period and to date and versus the Marketing Plan (the "Marketing Report").   
 
 3.2.7 Collection of Revenues.  Contractor shall collect from the System Users all 
fees owed for the use of the System by such System Users ("System Revenue").  Contractor 
shall provide to Co unty a quarterly report detailing the System Revenue collected by 
Contractor from System  Users and shall keep Co unty advised as to any delinquency in 
payment of fees by such System Users. 
 
 3.2.8 Revenue Audits.  Contractor shall maintain true and correct sets of books 
and records in connection with its accounting, billing, collection of fees under the User 
Agreements and payments made or forwarded to Co unty, and Contractor shall retain all 
such records for a period of not less than ten (10) years.  Co unty may, at its sole expense, 
from time to time and upon at least three (3) business days advance notice to Contractor 
audit all records of Contractor in connection with the costs , fees, and payments provided 
for in this Contract; provided that such audit will not cause a significant disruption in the 
operation of Contractor's business.  Such audit may also include an examination of 
Contractor's procedures and controls with respect to any costs, fees or payments provided 
for under this Contract.  Any overpayment or underpayment shown by such audit shall be 
promptly corrected.

ARTICLE 5 
CONSTRUCTION AND INSTALLATION SERVICES 
 
 5.1 Construction and Installation Services .  Contractor shall furnish all Materials, 
services, supervision, tools, equipment and supplies necessary to construct and install the System 
(collectively, the "Construction Services"), shall perform all Project Activities in accordance with 
the Progress Schedule and, unless otherwise directed by County, shall be required to proceed with 
the Project without undue delays or extended time intervals between Project Activities.  Contractor 
will therefore apply its resources to proceed with as many construction operations as possible, 
provided such activities are not inconsistent with the Progress Schedule and sound construction 
practices and methods. 
 
 5.2 Progress Schedule.  Attached hereto as Schedule 5 .2, Progress Schedule,  is a 
preliminary progress schedule for the Project that includes the Critical Path Milestones for the 
Project.   Contractor shall, within forty -five (45)  calendar days following the Effective D ate, 
submit for County's approval, a detailed progress schedule (" Progress Schedule") which, upon 
approval, shall replace the preliminary Progress Schedule and be attached hereto as Schedule 5.2, 
Progress Schedule.  The Progress Schedule shall include Crit ical Path Milestone dates for the 
design approval process described in Section 5.5, Proposed Design Plans; As-Built Plans.  The 
Progress Schedule shall include:  (a) Project milestone events; (b) the Critical Path Milestones and 
the commencement and comple tion dates for such Critical Path Milestones; (c) a detailed 
description of all Project Activities to be performed, including task and sub -task activities, the 
party responsible for, and the location of, on-site or off-site, such activities; and (d) a Construction 
Completion Date for the Project.  During the Project, County, from time to time, may cause 
Contractor to update the Progress Schedule; provided, however, that the dates specified in such 
Progress Schedule and approved by County shall not be modifi ed or extended at Contractor's 
request except for delays caused by a force majeure event as described in Section 14.6, Force 
Majeure Events or delays caused by the acts or omissions of County, and provided further that 
County may not shorten the length of time required to meet  any milestones respecting any 
Segment without the prior consent of Contractor.  Once any proposed revisions to a Progress 
Schedule are approved, the Progress Schedule shall be updated at least monthly to reflect such 
revisions and each such revised Progress Schedule shall replace the previous Progress Schedule 
and shall be deemed to be attached hereto as the replacement Schedule 5.2, Progress Schedule. 
 
  5.2.1 Acceleration. If, in the reasonable opinion of the County, Contractor has 
fallen behind the Progress Schedule for Construction Services, Contractor shall take such steps 
as may be reasonably required by the County, including but not limited to, increasing the number 
of personnel, shifts, and/or overtime operations, days of work, and/or amount of construction 
equipment until such time as the Construction Services are back on schedule, all at no additional 
cost to the County. 
 
 5.3 Inspection.  County shall have the right to inspect the progress of the Project, at 
any time, at the construction sites or at any other location at which Project Activities are occurring 
or will occur.  If, in County's reasonable opinion, the Construction Services, or other procedures 
or activities are incomplete, inadequate or not pertinent to the System or Construction Services 
furnished or to be furnished hereunder, Contractor shall be notified in writing, and Contractor shall 
correct the deficiency as soon as reasonably p racticable.  If, however, such deficiency is life 
threatening or a potential safety hazard, Contractor shall correct the deficiency immediately.

 5.6 Changes in Scope.  County and Contractor agree that it may be desirable to make

 ARTICLE 6 
CERTIFICATION PROCESS 
 
 6.1 Certification Tests.  Contractor shall perform Certification Tests for the System in 
accordance with the methods and criteria set forth in Schedule 2.1, Scope of Work  and shall be 
responsible for supplying any and all equipment that may be required or necessary to test the 
System and measure the results of such tests.  Contractor shall notify County in writing ten (10) 
business days in advance regarding the date, time and location of the Certification Tests and 
County may, at its option, be present at any or all Certification Tests.  In accordance with this 
Section 6.1, Certification Tests , County shall have the right to inspect the equipment and 
procedures being used to conduct the Certification Tests and the Certification Test results.  All

<!-- page 582 -->
-11-  
testing is to be directed to verify the operation and functionality of the System in accordance with 
the Technical Specifications. 
 
 6.2 Terms Applicable to Certification Tests. 
 
 6.2.1 Initiation of Tests .  Upon completion of all tasks that are prerequisite 
(according to the Progress Sched ule) to the corresponding Certification Test, Contractor 
shall notify County in writing that the relevant portion of the System is ready for 
Certification Testing. 
 
 6.2.2 Certification Tests by Contractor.  For each Certification Test: 
 
 (a) Statement of Installation.  Contractor shall present to the County 
Project Coordinator, for his or her review and approval, a Statement of Installation 
and Certification for each Segment of the System, which verifies the scope, 
methodologies, results of and participants in the applicable testing processes, as set 
forth in the Scope of Work.  Contractor shall also provide to County copies of any 
and all Certification Test data generated by Contractor in connection with the 
Certification Tests. 
 
 (b) Failure to Present Statement of Installation.  If Contractor fails to 
present a Statement of Installation and Certification to County by the end of the 
Certification period as defined in the Progress Schedule (or any retesting period as 
described in Section 6 .2.3, Retesting Procedure , below) then the pertinent 
Certification Tests shall be deemed unsuccessful with respect to such portion of the 
System. 
 
 (c) Segment Acceptance.  A Segment shall be accepted only when:  (i) 
all Materials are installed and certified; (ii) all As -Built Plans have been received 
and approved by County; and (iii) County notifies Contractor in writing that the 
results of the Certification Tests are acceptable, or County fails to notify Contractor 
of any rejection of the results of the Certification Tests within t en (10) business 
days of County's receipt of the Statement of Installation and Certification respecting 
a Segment.  Written notification by County that the Segment has passed the 
Certification Tests, all construction and installation tasks are completed for the 
applicable Segment and County has received all documentation required under this 
Contract (or the failure to deliver such notification within the time permitted herein) 
shall result in " Segment Acceptance."  The date upon which the final Segment 
Acceptance and Lateral Segment Acceptance has occurred shall be deemed to be 
the "System Acceptance Date". 
 
 6.2.3 Retesting Procedure. 
 
 (a) Subject to County's rights contained in this Contract, if a Segment 
is not accepted, or a part thereof fails to be accepted, County shall provide 
Contractor with a written list of discrepancies.  Contractor shall, within ten (10) 
business days after receipt of such list ei ther:  (i) modify or adjust the Segment to 
satisfy the applicable Documentation or begin to modify or adjust the Segment 
pursuant to a mutually agreed -upon plan to satisfy the applicable Documentation; 
or (ii) replace or add components or Materials as may be necessary to make the

<!-- page 583 -->
-12-  
Segment satisfy the applicable Documentation or begin to replace or add 
components or Materials pursuant to a mutually agreed -upon plan to make the 
Segment satisfy the applicable Documentation.  If the remedies under 
subparagraph (i) or (ii) above fail, then County shall have all rights and remedies 
provided in this Contract.  Upon completion of necessary adjustments or 
corrections, Contractor shall notify County in writing of the diagnosed problem, 
method for correction and readine ss of the Segment for re -execution of the 
applicable Certification Test process. 
 
 (b) If additional reported defects, non-conformities or discrepancies are 
found which were not known or were previously masked by the reported defects, 
non-conformities and/ or discrepancies, Contractor shall correct or commence to 
correct, pursuant to a mutually agreeable written corrective plan of action, such 
defects, non-conformities and/or discrepancies within five (5) business days and 
return such corrections to County for additional testing.  Subject to County's rights 
under Section 6.2.4, Failure to Attain Certification and Default For a Segment, 
this process of subsequent testing and correction shall repeat as necessary until all 
reported defects, non-conformities and/or discrepancies have been corrected. 
 
 6.2.4 Failure to Attain Certification and Default For a Segment .  
Notwithstanding any provision contained herein to the contrary, and subject to excused 
force majeure delays, if Segment Acceptance has not occurred within one hundred twenty 
(120) days after the scheduled date for Segment Acceptance as described in the Progress 
Schedule for the applicable Segment , County shall have the right to obtain any and all 
remedies identified in this Contract. 
 
ARTICLE 7

 7.1 Fiber Optic System Maintenance.  From and after the date of Segment Acceptance

System within such Segment in accordance with the requirements and procedures set forth in 
Schedule 7.1, Fiber Optic System Maintenance.  Such maintenance work will be performed by 
Contractor, or a Subcontractor chosen by Contractor to perform the work.   
 
 7.2 The costs of Scheduled Maintenance (as such term is defined in Schedule 7.1, 
Fiber Optic System Maintenance), shall be borne by Contractor as part of the Maintenance Fee;

Maintenance (as such term is defined in Schedule 7.1, Fiber Optic System Maintenance ).  
Contractor will send County invoices for the Maintenance Fee and for any for any Unscheduled 
Maintenance work, and County shall pay such invoices, in accordance with the procedures 
described in Section 3.1.2, Other Payments. 
 
 7.3 Maintenance Fee.  In consideration for Contractor's performance of Scheduled 
Maintenance of the System, County shall pay to Contractor the annual Maintenance Fee, invoiced 
and payable in advance, during the Term.  Recognizing that Segments will be accepted at different 
times, the Maintenance Fee shall be pro -rated accordingly on a Segment-by-Segment basis until 
the System Acceptance Date, at which time the entire Maintenance Fee shall be due and payable

Maintenance Fee any pre -paid fees for individual Segments that extend beyond the System

Acceptance Date).  The Maintenance Fee shall be increased on each anniversary of the System

discretion, designate a successor index to be used in determining any increase to the Maintenance 
Fee. 
 
 7.4 Relocations.  If, after the System Acceptance Date, the System, or a portion thereof, 
must be relocated due to the order of any Governmental Authority or any other Person having the

or its designated Subcontractor, shall perform the relocation work in accordance with the process 
described in Section 5.7, Changes in Scope, recognizing that County shall be solely responsible

of this Contract.

ARTICLE 12 
DISPUTE RESOLUTION 
 
 12.1 Performance Review.  Subject to the terms of Section 12.6, Equitable Relief, the 
procedures of this Article 12, Dispute Resolution , shall control the resolution of any and all 
disputes that might arise between the parties and that are related to this Contract.  The parties shall 
first seek to resolve each dispute at the Project Manager and County Project Coordinator level as 
described below in Section 12.2, Project Coordinator/Project Director Level Performance 
Review; if good faith negotiations at that level are unsuccessful in resolving such dispute, then the 
parties shall attempt to resolve the dispute at the Executive Level as described in Section 12.3, 
Executive Level Performance Review; if good faith negotiations at that level are unsuccessful in 
resolving such dispute,  then the parties may mutually agree to resolve the dispute through 
mediation as described in Section 12.4, Non-Binding Mediation; if mediation is not successful 
in resolving such dispute, then the parties may each pursue any remedy available at law or in 
equity.  Notwithstanding the foregoing, if good faith negotiations at the Executive Level, as 
described in Section 12.3, Executive Level Performance Review are not successful, either party 
may file suit in a court of competent jurisdiction in accordance wi th the terms of this Contract, 
provided that non-binding mediation, pursuant to Section 12.4, Non-Binding Mediation has not 
been agreed to by the parties and/or is not then pending.  
 
 12.2 Project Coordinator/Project Manager Level Performance Review .  The Project 
Manager and the County Project Coordinator shall meet as often as shall reasonably be requested 
by either party to review the performance of either party under this Contract and to resolve the 
dispute.  Written minutes of such meetings shall be kept. 
 
 12.3 Executive Level Performance  Review.  Face-to-face negotiations shall be 
conducted by an executive officer of County and the President or Chief Operations Officer of 
Contractor.  If such representatives are unable to resolve the dispute between the parties within ten 
(10) business days after the initial request for negotiations at this level (or such period as the parties 
shall otherwise agree), or thirty (30) calen dar days have passed since the initial request for 
negotiations at this level, then the parties may mutually agree in writing to resolve the dispute by 
mediation as set forth in Section 12.4, Non-Binding Mediation. 
 
 12.4 Non-Binding Mediation .  If the par ties agree to pursue non -binding mediation, 
then such mediation should be scheduled as promptly as is reasonably practicable after 
negotiations under Section 12.3, Executive Level Performance Review , have been terminated.  
The parties shall mutually select an independent mediator experienced in information systems and 
telecommunications disputes and shall each designate a representative to meet with the mediator 
in good faith in an effort to resolve the dispute.  The specific format for the mediation shall be left

<!-- page 590 -->
-19-  
to the discretion of the mediator and the designated representatives and may include the preparation 
of agreed upon statements of fact or written statements of position furnished to the other party.  If 
good faith mediation under this Section 12.4,  Non-Binding Mediation , is unsuccessful in 
resolving the dispute within thirty (30) calendar days after commencement, then the parties shall 
each be entitled to pursue any remedy available to them at law or in equity.   
 
 12.5 Equitable Relief .  Notwithsta nding anything contained in this Contract to the 
contrary, the parties shall be entitled to seek injunctive or equitable relief whenever the facts or 
circumstances would permit a party to seek such relief in a court of competent jurisdiction.

SCHEDULE 2.1 
 
SCOPE OF WORK 
 
1. General 
 
Contractor shall perform all construction activities in a workmanlike manner in accordance 
with approved Proposed Design Plans, As-Built Plans and Technical Specifications.   
 
2. System Description 
 
The System shall consist of two backbone routes and the laterals as shown and identified in 
Schedule 5.4 Image 5.4-1 Route Overview Map and Schedule 5.4 Lateral List. The primary 
backbone route of the network is comprised of five (5) Segments and consists of 
approximately 396,000 ft. of 288-count single mode fiber that will be installed 100% 
underground in a new 1.25” duct with a second spare 1.25” duct running from close 
proximity of the APS Cholla Power Plant near Joseph City south to Pinetop-Lakeside 
terminating near the Fort Apache Indian Reservation border.  All preliminary plans and 
routes are subject to change based final design and field conditions.  
 
Segment 1 of the network originates at an access point near the APS Cholla Power Plant and 
runs east along I-40 to Holbrook and terminates at an access point near the Summit 
Healthcare Specialty Clinic. 
 
Segment 2 runs from the Summit Healthcare Specialty Clinic and turns south along Highway 
77 towards Snowflake and Taylor where it will terminate at an access point near the 
Snowflake Taylor Police Department.   
 
Segment 3 runs from Snowflake passing through Taylor and Shumway along Highway 77.  
The network will continue west and southwest on Lone Pine Dam Rd. approximately seven 
(7) miles north of Show Low to avoid a largely Basalt rock plateau.  From Lone Pine Dam 
Rd., the network will continue south to Highway 260 and back into Show Low from the west 
side along old Linden Rd. and Deuce of Clubs Ave. where it will terminate in an access point 
near the intersection with Highway 260.   
 
Segment 4 runs from Show Low and will continue south on Highway 260 through Lakeside 
and to Pinetop where it will terminate in an access point near the Summit Health Pinetop 
Medical facility.   
 
Segment 5 runs from Pinetop along Highway 260 where it terminates near the Fort Apache 
Indian Reservation border. 
 
The secondary backbone route of the network is comprised of one segment which consists of 
approximately 156,000 ft. of 288-count single mode fiber installed 100% underground in a 
new 1.25” duct with a second spare 1.25” duct running from Show Low to Heber-Overgaard.  
Segment 6 originates at Highway 260 and the intersection with the Lone Pine Dam Rd. 
segment from the primary backbone.  The segment heads west on Highway 260 to Heber-
Overgaard where it will terminate at an access point near the intersection of Highway 260 
and Highway 277.

-2-

identified below and shown in Schedule 5.4 Lateral List.  Laterals will include a ¾” SDR 11 
HDPE duct populated with a 12-count single mode fiber cable.
