3. Documentation of the Work 
 
Contractor shall deliver to County a complete and accurate final design submittal and final 
as-built submittal.  For each submittal Contractor will provide One (1) electronic copy in GIS 
compatible file format and One (1) electronic PDF print. 
 
4. Technical Specifications 
 
The Work shall meet the following technical specifications.  The specifications are generally 
accepted industry standard for an underground fiber optic communications infrastructure.   
 
• Conduit will be 1.25” (for duct) or .75”  (for laterals) HDPE SDR 11.  The conduit 
will allow for the installation of a single-mode 288 count fiber optic cable or smaller.  
The conduits will be contiguous throughout the System.  Conduits will be color coded 
for identification purposes. 
• Conduits will be installed at a depth of not less than 36” below finished grade unless 
soil and ground conditions require less depth. 
• Conduit installed under roadways will be installed at a depth of no less than 36” 
below finished grade. 
• The conduits shall be direct buried and backfilled with select material. 
• All underground conduit will be installed in the most practical location allowed by 
the permitting jurisdiction.

<!-- page 602 -->
-3- 
 
• Underground conduits shall be installed utilizing the plowing, directional boring and 
trenching methods of construction.  
Contractor accepts no responsibility for rock or other subsurface obstructions.  In the event rock 
or other subsurface obstructions are encountered, work shall stop, and Contractor shall consult 
with County to determine potential alternative construction methods (e.g., installing conduit at a 
depth less than 36”) prior to proceeding with construction through rock or other subsurface 
obstructions .   Additional cost associated with rock or other subsurface obstruction shall be 
completed first utilizing the rock adder allowance and then on a time and materials basis at the 
unit rate set forth in Schedule 3.1 if the adder has been fully utilized.  The process for adding 
such additional rock adder quantity shall be in accordance with Section 5.6, Changes in Scope. 
•  
• All conduits shall be proofed following installation to remove obstructions and 
confirm at least 90 percent of the nominal conduit diameter.  A proofing log shall be 
maintained to document that each span (handhole to handhole) proofed successfully.  
• A warning ribbon will be buried during the plow and trench operations approximately 
12” above the conduit.  The warning ribbon shall bear cautionary wording indicating 
the presence of a fiber optic cable. 
• If bridge attachments are required, 5” PVC conduit (or other suitable lower cost 
material) will be utilized for bridge crossings.  Expansion joints will be installed at 
appropriate intervals to allow for expansion and contraction of the conduit.  The 
conduit will be attached to the bridge with industry standard bridge attachment 
hardware.  The pipe hangers will be attached to the bridge with appropriate hardware.  
1.25” corrugated HDPE conduit will be installed inside the 5” PVC. 
• All conduits will be capped after installation.  Conduits will be water-tight sealed 
after fiber installation.   
• Handholes will be installed at appropriate intervals of approximately 2000 to 2,500 
feet.  Handholes will be placed at predetermined locations, including each side of 
bridge crossings, at major intersections and near all County facilities. 
• Handholes of an appropriate size with Tier 15 Lids will installed at all splice 
locations. 
• All handholes will be buried to grade with lids flush to the surface of the ground. 
• All handholes will be bottomless and set on top of a 12” pea gravel base for drainage 
with rodent screen or the equivalent. 
• Warning marker posts will be placed at intervals of approximately 1,000 feet along 
the route.  Warning markers will be placed at all changes in direction of the conduit 
system, splice locations, handhole locations and at both sides of street, highway and 
railroad crossings.  Markers will be positioned so that they can be seen from the 
location of the cable and generally facing perpendicular to the cable running line.  In 
general, the writing on the warning markers will be “Caution: Fiber Optic Cable 
Buried Below.” 
• Locate posts will be placed at each splice location.  The fiber cable will be grounded 
and connected to the locate post for locating purposes.  The locate post will service as 
an access point to isolate the sheath of the fiber optic cable and also as a grounding 
point.  The locate post will allow easy access for the connection of electric 
underground cable locating equipment.  The locate post shall be a poly post route

<!-- page 603 -->
-4- 
 
marker or a sheath isolation pedestal (SIP).  The locate post shall include a terminal 
equipped with three lugs.  Two of the lugs will be used to terminate the insulated 
copper ground wire.  The third lug will be used to terminate an insulated copper 
ground wire leading to and connected to a copper ground rod installed in the 
immediate vicinity. 
• The 288 count FOC will single-mode, loose-tube and armored, unless otherwise 
specified in the design drawings.  Manufacturer warranties will be included. 
• Fiber optic cables will be installed primarily using the blowing method. 
• Minimum slack coils of 50 feet will be placed in all handholes. 
• All laterals will be built to parcel property line with fiber cable coiled and placed in 
handhole at property line. 
• All fibers will be OTDR tested after installation.  Results will exceed TIA/EIA 
Standards.  Fiber will have a maximum attenuation of 0.25 dB/KM at 1550 nm.   
 
5. Design  
 
Contractor will design the System.  Contractor will develop a complete design to provide an 
underground fiber optic system.  The design will include a complete set of material 
specifications and all drawings necessary to construct the system. The drawings package will 
include the running line for the proposed route, splicing diagrams and typical drawings for 
installation.  The route drawings will be drafted electronically using GIS platform and made 
suitable for printing to PDF and utilized for construction drawings.  The typical installation 
detail drawings will be developed in AutoCAD and delivered electronically in PDF format.  
The drawings will adhere to applicable County and NEC specifications as well as safety 
codes.  
 
During the outside plant design process, Contractor will work with the County to ensure all 
route options are analyzed and potential future connections to County facilities are 
considered.  Long-term maintenance considerations will be taken into account when 
designing the System. 
 
County will issue a blanket permit for all construction on its ROW.  County will not charge a 
permit fee.  Contractor will work with other permitting entities for all construction conducted 
off County ROW.  County will be responsible for all permit fees associated with construction 
off the County ROW.    
 
In order to keep the project design moving along efficiently the process described below will 
be utilized.  Each step is described in more detail below 
  
 
50% Design  
 
The 50% design will consist of the following tasks and deliverables. 
 
• Meet with County staff to review project goals and gather key information required 
for the design such as ROW limits, list of County facilities planned for future 
connection, as-built drawings of existing facilities, review construction specifications

<!-- page 604 -->
-5- 
 
and discuss long-term construction projects that may impact System construction or 
maintenance.   
• Conduct a desktop review of County ROW to choose or discuss alternate running 
lines. 
• Generate a preliminary fiber route layout. 
• Prepare a preliminary list of permitting entities for all work off of the County ROW. 
• Detailed field engineering to determine running line. 
• Generate initial route drawings in GIS. 
• Prepare logs for all required permits. 
• Make initial contact with permitting entities to determine requirements. 
• Develop initial bill of materials 
• Complete permit applications and submit to permitting entities. 
• Meet with permitting entities as required. 
• Prepare any detail drawings required for permits. 
• Layout fiber cable, identify splice points and create splicing diagrams. 
• Develop construction typical drawings. 
• Finalize bill of materials. 
 
100% Design 
 
The 100% design will consist of the following tasks and deliverables. 
 
• Incorporate final comments from permitting entities into drawing package. 
• Pay any applicable permit fees (County responsible for payment). 
• Obtain Professional Engineer stamp if required. 
• Submit Approved for Construction Drawings to County. 
 
6. Conduit Installation Practices 
 
a. General.  Contractor shall be familiar with general guidelines covering the 
construction of buried communications cable and Section 641 of the REA 
Telephone Engineering and Construction Manual. 
The equipment and construction methods used by Contractor shall be such as to 
cause minimum displacement of the soil. 
 
Where innerduct/cable is buried near the edge of pavements, Contractor shall take 
particular care to avoid damaging the pavement.  If such damage does occur, repair 
shall be made immediately to meet the complete satisfaction of state or local 
authorities having jurisdiction over the pavement. 
 
b. Plowing Equipment Requirements.  Pre-ripping is not a prerequisite to 
innerduct/cable placement on this project.  Pre-ripping, as determined, of the buried 
cable route shall precede plowing, and shall be made in the same direction as 
innerduct/cable is to be plowed, at a depth of four inches (4") greater than the 
minimum cable depth required.

<!-- page 605 -->
-6- 
 
 
The cable plow tractor and pull tractor, if required, shall each be capable of 
delivering a minimum of fifty-five thousand pounds (55,000 lbs.) (2.45 X 105 N) 
drawbar pull at 1.2 MPH (1.93 KM/hr) forward speed to bury the innerduct/cable at 
the specified depth in soil.  Under certain soil conditions, it is likely that a pull 
tractor shall be required.  The additional requirement shall be made at the discretion 
of the Contractor’s Construction Manager or his designee.   
 
A prime mover with hydrostatic steering and a static plow shall perform plowing of 
all fiber cable. 
 
The design of the plowshare shall be such that the innerduct or buried cable passing 
through the plow will not bind and shall not be bent in a radius less than twenty 
(20) times the outside diameter of the cable or innerduct.  The feed chute must be 
a removable gate for the purpose of inspection and to allow the cable to be removed 
from or inserted into the feed chute at any intermediate point between splice 
locations.  The cable path inside the feed chute must have low friction surfaces and 
be free of burrs and sharp edges, to prevent damage to the cable as it passes 
through.  Any welds must be smoothed.  Internal guide rollers shall not be used. 
 
The equipment shall be capable of extending the plow, in order to maintain the 
required minimum depths under all terrain conditions. 
 
The reel carrier shall be of adequate size and be configured so that the reel sizes 
being used can be safely handled. 
 
c. Plowing Requirements.  The slot made in the soil by the cable plows shall be closed 
immediately by driving a vehicle track of sufficient weight over the plow slot to 
thoroughly compact the plow slot, or by other suitable means as determined by 
Contractor.  This requires three (3) passes with a track machine, one (1) on each 
side and one (1) down the middle.  A vibratory roller having a weight of three (3) 
tons and a width of four to six feet (4’-6’) may also be used. 
 
Start and finish pits and pits at points of intersections, as needed, must be excavated 
in advance of plowing cable.  Ends of casings and crossings of foreign utilities shall 
be exposed prior to start of cable plowing operations. 
 
Contractor shall exercise particular care in the use of trenching equipment and 
shovels in joining trenches to the slot made by the plow, to be certain that the 
innerduct/cable is not damaged. 
 
To avoid possible damage to buried innerduct/cable from exposure to traffic, 
livestock, and other hazards, trenching of laterals, trenching around culverts, 
construction of aerial inserts and similar operations shall be completed as soon as 
feasible behind the plow operation. 
 
Care is to be exercised during the plowing operation to feed the innerduct/cable into 
the ground through the plow.  Equipment and construction methods shall be such as 
to assure compliance with this requirement.  Contractor shall furnish competent

<!-- page 606 -->
-7- 
 
supervision at all times at the site of plowing operations, to assure compliance with 
this requirement. 
 
Innerducts shall be placed through the chute with some tension to allow the 
innerduct to be installed straight.  Effort shall be made to insure the innerduct does 
not twist or roll during the plowing operation. 
 
If, during the plowing operation, the plow should strike a buried object or rock that 
stops the equipment and necessitates removal of the plow from the ground, the 
precautions detailed in this section shall be observed to avoid damage to the 
innerduct/cable. 
 
Where casing pipe or foreign utility is encountered, innerduct may be cut at the sole 
discretion of the Contractor.  All intermediate innerduct splices shall be fused so as 
to maintain at least 90% of the original inner diameter.  Pressed couplers may also 
be utilized.  After the cable is pulled through the casing pipe(s) or under the foreign 
utilities, it shall be replaced on the reel, and the plowing operation restarted.  
EXTREME CARE will be used whenever the cable is handled, so that it will not be 
kinked or damaged in any manner. 
 
Warning Tape shall be installed with twelve inches (12”) of cover. 
 
At no time shall any reels be unmanned during cable installation. 
 
d. Plowing Precautions.  Failure to observe precautions concerning proper operation 
of the prime mover and plow contributes to unnecessary cable/innerduct damages.  
The following precautions shall be reviewed with equipment operators and shall be 
strictly observed. 
 
• The tractor shall always be started slowly, and speed increased gradually 
after all cable is removed from the cable delivery system. 
 
• Plow altitude and depth shall be changed gradually.  Such changes shall be 
made while prime mover is moving. 
 
• Should it be necessary to raise the plow shear to the surface when the plow 
is not moving, the cable to the rear of the feed chute shall be excavated and 
slack pulled so that the cable is not kinked over the feed chute exit. 
 
• Do not plow with the shear set at extreme forward rake angles without a 
shear specifically designed for this purpose. 
 
• When rigging for off-set plowing, the cable shall be re-routed over the cable 
feed systems to conform to the new configuration. 
 
• Abrupt changes in the terrain along the cable path shall be graded off ahead 
of the plow, if possible.

<!-- page 607 -->
-8- 
 
• The plowing operation shall be observed continuously for obstructions, 
proper feeding of the cable, maintaining proper depth, etc. 
 
• Under no circumstances shall the plow be backed, or the shear moved to the 
rear with cable in the chute. 
 
• At no time shall the plow be wobbled, either vertically or horizontally, to 
break through an obstruction. 
 
• At no time shall the plow deviate from the normal route to seek an "on 
grade" crossing level for farm roads.  Unless the road is bored, Contractor 
shall level the plow train path in order to make a level crossing of the road.  
Contractor shall repair the road after passage, including re-paving or 
graveling, as required. 
 
• No practice will be allowed that will cause an abrupt change in direction of 
the plowed-in cable. 
 
• Sufficient equipment and manpower will be available to make sure the 
innerducts are fed through the shoot straight and with proper tension. 
 
e. Trench Installation – Trenching shall be done where plowing is not feasible.  
Excavation shall be performed to install innerducts to allow a minimum thirty-six 
inches (36”) of cover below finished grade.  The installation shall be complete with 
the removal and disposal of excess excavated materials or materials not suitable for 
backfill and the installation of the conduit.  The work shall also include shoring, 
bracing, dewatering, manhole entrances, road bore connections, and all other 
operations necessary to complete the installation.  Surface conditions shall be 
restored with necessary topsoil and grass seed. 
 
Trenches shall be kept as straight as practical.  The bottom of the trench shall be 
smooth and free from any sharp edges.  The trench shall be kept clear of debris and 
loose rock.  All changes in trench grade shall be gradual.  Conduits shall be placed 
in the center of the excavation and as straight as practical.  Where conduits cross 
existing sub-surface utilities, the conduits shall be placed to maintain a minimum of 
twelve inches (12”) of clearance from the object, if possible.   
 
f. Street Trench Installation – Contractor shall excavate as necessary to install the 
conduit system with a minimum twenty-four inches (24”) of cover below finished 
grade or as shown on the construction drawings.  The installation shall be 
complete with saw cutting the roadway surfaces, removal and disposal of 
excavated roadway surface and excess excavated material and the installation of 
the conduit. Restoration shall be made in accordance the specifications of the 
appropriate permitting agency. Temporary asphalt restoration will be required 
when vehicular traffic will be present prior to final asphalt restoration.  
Temporary asphalt restoration will include placing cold patch in the trench, and 
compaction to finished grade.  Steel plating may be used for temporary closure 
and must be at least ¾ inch thick and shall be pinned and the edge tapered with 
temporary asphalt.

<!-- page 608 -->
-9- 
 
 
Final roadway surface restoration shall conform to the specifications of the 
applicable jurisdictional authority. 
 
Trenches shall be kept as straight as practical.  The bottom of the trench shall be 
smooth and free from any sharp edges.  The trench shall be kept clear of debris and 
loose rock.  All changes in trench grade shall be gradual.  All trench sections must 
be closed at the end of each working day.  Conduits shall be placed in the center of 
the excavation and as straight as practicable. 
  
Driveways, lanes, or roadways, which are open cut, shall be opened just prior to the 
conduit placing.  In no case shall the driveway, lane, or roadway be left impassable 
at the end of the day.  The general public safety is paramount and appropriate steps 
shall be taken to ensure safety at all times.  Where a drive or roadway must be left 
open for traffic, the subcontractor must provide the material and method required to 
allow for movement of traffic.  Steel plating may be used for temporary closure 
and must be at least ¾ inch thick and shall be pinned and the edge tapered with 
temporary asphalt.  
 
Trenches shall be promptly backfilled with earth and suitable means tamped so that 
the earth is restored to original grade to assure no hazard to vehicular, animal or 
pedestrian traffic. All open trenches will be properly guarded or barricaded to 
prevent damage or injury. 
 
In general, the select backfill shall consist of unfrozen material free of rock and 
other debris.  Material previously removed from the trench will qualify as select 
backfill.   
 
When pipe or conduit is placed by trenched construction beneath a roadway or a 
driveway or within five feet of the edge of an existing or proposed pavement or 
base course, the backfill within the roadway shall be placed and compacted in 
accordance with the requirements of the authority having jurisdiction. 
 
In areas inaccessible to tamping type rollers where compaction is required, a 
mechanical tamper of a size suitable for the work involved shall be used.  
Pneumatic tampers shall be operated at pressures no less than those recommended 
by the manufacturer. 
 
g. Horizontal Directional Drilling – The directional boring equipment shall consist 
of a directional boring machine of sufficient capacity to perform the bore and 
pullback the conduit(s), a boring fluid mixing and delivery system of sufficient 
capacity to successfully complete the crossing, a guidance system to accurately 
guide boing operations and trained and competent personnel to operate the 
system.  All equipment shall be in good, safe operating condition with sufficient 
supplies, materials and spare parts on hand to maintain the system in good 
working order for the duration of the work. 
 
 The directional boring machine shall consist of a hydraulically powered system to 
rotate, push and pull hollow drill pipe into the ground a variable angle while 
delivering a pressurized fluid mixture to a guidance drill (bore) head.  The

<!-- page 609 -->
-10- 
 
machine shall be anchored to the ground to withstand the pulling, pushing and 
rotating pressure required to the complete the crossing.  The Hydraulic system 
shall be free of leaks.  The boring machine shall have a system to monitor and 
record maximum pull-back pressure during pull-back operations.  The boring 
machine shall be grounded during boring and pull-back operations.  
 
 The bore head shall be steerable by changing its rotation and shall provide the 
necessary cutting surfaces and boring fluid jets. 
 
 Mud motors shall be of adequate power to turn the required boring tools. 
 
 Drill pipes shall be constructed of high quality 4130 seamless tubing, grade D or 
better, with threaded box and pins.  Tool joints should be hardened to 32-36 RC. 
 
 The guidance system shall be of a proven type and shall be setup and operated by 
personnel trained and experienced with the system.  The operator shall be aware 
of any magnetic anomalies and shall consider such influences in the operation of 
the guidance system if using a magnetic system.   
  
 A self-contained, closed, boring fluid mixing system shall be of sufficient size to 
mix and deliver boring fluid composed of bentonite clay, potable water and 
appropriate additives.  Mixing system shall be able to molecularly shear 
individual bentonite particles from the dry powder to avoid clumping and ensure 
thorough mixing.  Mixing shall continuously agitate the boring fluid during 
boring operations. 
 
 Drilling fluid shall be composed of clean water and an appropriate additive.  
Water shall be from a clean source with a pH of 8.5-10.  Water of a lower pH or 
with excessive calcium shall be treated with the appropriate amount of sodium 
carbonate or equal.  The water and additives shall be mixed thoroughly and be 
absent of any clumps or clods.  No hazardous additives may be used.  Boring fluid 
shall be maintained at a viscosity sufficient to suspend cutting and maintain the 
integrity of bore wall. 
 
 The entire drill path shall be accurately inspected with entry and exit stakes 
placed in the appropriate locations as indicated on the drawings.  If a magnetic 
guidance system is utilized, the drill path shall be surveyed for any surface geo-
magnetic variations or anomalies.   
 
 A silt fence shall be placed between all boring operations and any drainage, 
wetland, waterway or other area designated for such protection by the drawings.   
 
 Bore pipe shall be connected together in one length prior to pull-back operations 
if space permits.  Steel pipe welds will be X-rayed prior to being placed in bore 
hole.  Pipe will be placed on a pipe roller before pulling into bore hole with rollers 
spaced close enough to prevent excessive sagging of pipe. 
 
 A pilot hole shall be drilled on bore path with no deviations greater than 5% of 
depth over a length of 100 feet.  Any deviations shall be preapproved by 
Contractor.

<!-- page 610 -->
-11- 
 
 
 A frack out plan will be in place prior to the commencement of any directional 
boring operations.  In the event that a boring fluid fracture inadvertent returns or 
returns loss occurs during pilot hole boring operations, work shall cease for at 
least 30 minutes.  After 30 minutes have elapsed, boring fluid with viscosity 
exceeding 120 seconds as measured by a March funnel will be injected and work 
will cease for an additional 30 minutes.  If mud fracture or returns loss continues, 
work will cease until a revised plan is developed. 
 
 Upon successful completion of pilot hole, a bore hole will be reamed to a 
minimum of 25% greater than outside diameter of pipe. 
 
 After successfully reaming the bore hole to the required diameter, conduit(s) shall 
be pulled back through the bore bole.  In front of the pipe will be a swivel.  Once 
pull back operations have commenced, operations must continue without 
interruption until pipe is completely pulled into bore hole.  During pull back 
operations, the maximum safe pipe pull pressure shall not be exceeded at any 
time.  Effort shall be made to insure the innerduct does not twist or roll during the 
pullback operation. 
 
 In the event the pipe becomes stuck, pulling operations shall cease to allow any 
potential hydro-lock to subside. 
 
7. Cable Installation 
 
Contractor shall install the FOC into a HDPE duct along the route.  Contractor shall install 
the cable by the blowing method for the majority of the route.  Pulling cable may be 
utilized for shorter installations. 
 
a. Cable Blowing Installation.  Contractor shall install cable by the blowing method 
using industry standard equipment.  All manufacturer guidelines for the 
installation of fiber cable shall be followed. 
 
b. Innerduct Installation.  Not applicable 
 
c. Cable Installation.  Handholes are located approximately every 2000 to 2,500 feet.  
The FOC reel lengths will be cut to install between handholes and are designated as 
such on the route drawings.  Each cable installation shall be planned in accordance 
with the information about splice locations, conduit layout, handhole locations, etc. 
to optimize existing handholes for splice locations.    
 
Bends of small radii and twists that may damage the fiber optic cable shall be 
avoided.  During cable placement, cable shall not be bent in a radius less than 
twenty (20) times the outside diameter of the cable.  Pulleys, sheaves or radius 
wheels shall be used to meet this requirement. 
 
Cable shall not be pulled with more than six hundred pounds (600 lbs.) of dynamic 
tension.  Safeguards such as a break-away swivel and adjustable slip clutch capstan 
winch or pulling dynamometer shall be used.

<!-- page 611 -->
-12- 
 
Cable lubrication shall be used to reduce the pulling tension on all segments of the 
cable placement operation.  Recommended lubricant is Polywater F, or an approved 
equivalent. 
 
If necessary, additional handholes may be added to the System to facilitate cable 
installation.  All new handholes locations shall be documented on the redline 
drawings and included in the final as-built drawings.  A 100-foot slack loop will 
be placed in every handhole, or as designated on the drawings.  
 
d. Placing Cable at Reel Ends.  The cable will be placed to provide sufficient cable for 
splicing at ground level.  A minimum of 50feet of cable slack on each side of the 
splice will be left in splice handholes. 
 
e. Handhole Racking.  All FOC shall be racked in the handholes in accordance with 
industry practice.  Slack coils shall be neatly coiled and securely attached to the 
rack in each handhole. 
 
8. Splicing and Certification Testing 
 
FOC shall be spliced using fusion splicing techniques.  Fusion splicing equipment shall be 
cleaned, calibrated and adjusted to the fiber and environmental conditions at the start of the 
work and shall checked daily and adjusted, as necessary.  Splicing includes opening the 
cable, splicing the fibers using the fusion splicing technique, placing a heat shrink on the bare 
fiber splice, loading the spliced fiber in a splice tray, labeling each splice tray and placing 
each of the splice trays in the splice enclosure, closing the splice enclosure, placing the splice 
enclosure in the handhole, neatly coiling the excess cable in the handhole and placing the 
securing the handhole lid.   
 
The average splice loss for each bi-directional OTDR tested splice shall not exceed 0.30 dB 
bi-directionally.  Three (3) attempts shall be made on an individual splice to reach the 
maximum bi-directional average splice loss.  If the maximum bi-directional, average loss has 
not been achieved after the third attempt, the splice shall be approved and tagged as out of 
spec. 
 
All fibers shall be tested using an OTDR at 1550 nm.  Each fiber shall be tested 
independently.  All test equipment shall be in good working order and shall have been 
calibrated prior to testing being conducted.  
 
All test results shall be documented and provide to County in electronic format.  All fiber 
tests shall be documented in both directions.  An access jumper (launch reel) that allows 
viewing of the entire cable length shall be utilized.  The documentation shall include the date 
and time the test was performed, the cable being tested, and equipment used to complete the 
test and the results of the tests. 
 
Optical attenuation shall be measured with a power meter on all fibers uni-directionally using 
the insertion loss method.  A launch reel shall be used at the transmit and receive ends to 
ensure accurate measurements. 
 
The entire fiber optic system shall be properly protected from foreign voltage and grounded 
with industry accepted system.

<!-- page 612 -->
-13- 
 
 
9. Protection of Existing Utilities 
 
Contractor shall take all necessary precautions to safeguard existing utilities.  Contractor 
shall submit proper notification to the appropriate state “One Call” agency and to the County 
prior to any excavation activities.  Contractor shall allow ample time in the schedule to 
ensure all utilities have been located accurately.    Contractor shall obtain the location of all 
buried utilities prior to performing any excavation.   All perpendicular crossings of the 
proposed conduit system shall be potholed to verify actual locations.  All parallel utilities 
within three feet of the proposed conduit system shall be potholed to verify actual location.  
At all times Contractor shall be responsible to protect all adjacent utilities during the 
excavations and back-fill process.    
 
All utility damages shall be reported to County, the local “One Call” agency, utility owner 
and local authorities (as required) immediately.  A utility damage report will be submitted to 
County within 24 hours. 
 
County shall be responsible for completing all locates for County owned underground 
utilities in a timely manner.   
 
Contractor shall not be responsible for damage to un-located underground utilities, or utilities 
marked outside of the standard tolerance zone as recognized by the local “One Call” agency. 
 
10. Existing Fences 
 
Fences on the ROW shall not be removed without approval by the County.  Contractor may 
remove fences where necessary for the performance of the work and shall rebuild them in as 
good condition as found.  Where designated, fences shall be maintained until the work is 
completed or their removal is authorized.  Where Contractor removed existing fences to 
facilitate work, temporary fence protection shall be adequate to prevent livestock from 
straying from or onto adjacent lands and shall be constructed complete with gates and or 
cattle guards as applicable.  Temporary fencing constructed on the ROW shall be removed by 
Contractor as part of the clean-up operation prior to final acceptance of the completed work. 
 
11. Clean-Up and Disposal of Waste Materials 
 
Contractor shall at all times keep the construction area free from accumulation of waste 
materials.   
 
Prior to completion of the work, Contractor shall remove equipment, materials and waste 
used during construction of the System.  All work areas shall be graded and left in a neat 
manner conforming to the natural appearance of the landscape.  All disturbed areas will be 
restored with seed and matting. 
 
All waste materials shall be removed from the construction area and disposed of by 
Contractor.  Waste materials removed from the construction site shall be disposed in a 
manner and at approved waste disposal sites.  It shall be the responsibility of Contractor to 
make all necessary arrangements with private or public entities for waste disposal.   
Contractor will be responsible for any fees or charges related to the disposal of materials.  All 
waste materials are the property of Contractor until properly disposed of.

<!-- page 613 -->
-14- 
 
 
 
 
12. Safety 
 
Contractor shall at all times perform all work in the safest possible manner.  Daily safety 
meetings shall be conducted with all personnel present at the job site.  Safety meetings shall 
also be conducted anytime there is a change in job conditions.  Safety inspections of the work 
site shall be conducted prior to the commencement of any work activity. 
 
All personnel working on the project shall be trained to perform their job functions.  
Contractor shall ensure that all personnel have and are properly utilizing the appropriate 
tools, safety devices and personal protective equipment to perform all work activities.  
Contractor shall adhere to all federal, state, local and OSHA safety requirements at all times. 
 
All accidents shall be reported to County immediately.  An accident report shall be 
completed and submitted to County within 24 hours. 
 
13. Materials 
Contractor will be responsible for ordering, delivering, acceptance and securing storing of all 
materials required for the System.  County will provide space along the ROW to stage 
materials.   
 
14. Documentation of the Work 
 
Contractor shall deliver to County complete and accurate as-built drawings.  One (1) 
electronic copy shall be provided to the County.

SCHEDULE 3.2.3 
 
SHARING OF SYSTEM REVENUES 
 
System Revenue.  Contractor and County shall share System Revenue generated by Contractor's 
marketing and promotion of the System as follows:   
Contractor shall receive fifteen percent (15%) of all IRU Fees .  The remaining eighty-five 
percent (85%) of such IRU Fees shall be paid to County in accordance with the provisions of 
Article 3.2.3.   
County shall receive one hundred percent (100%) of any Operations and Maintenance Fees paid 
by System Users.  
 
Fees for Unscheduled Maintenance shall be billed to the County and all System Users on a pro-
rata basis determined by the number of fibers owned by each.  
 
Marketing Services. 
Contractor will perform the following marketing duties, as more fully described in the Marketing 
Plan: 
• Create co-branded print and digital marketing collateral that depicts the System, egress 
point locations and availability of assets. 
• Advertise the System with various trade associations, dark fiber user groups and 
additional carriers and ILECs. 
• Create and share content on Contractor’s social media platforms (LinkedIn, Facebook, 
Twitter) to drive interested parties to the County’s and Contractor’s websites, as 
applicable, and promote attendance and face-to-face meetings at scheduled industry 
conferences. 
• Incorporate public relations initiatives to promote community awareness through press 
releases, media advisories and community educational sessions, if desired. 
 
Sales/Business Development Services. 
Contractor will develop the pricing structure for fiber, duct and maintenance user fees, using 
industry-based research.  
Contractor will utilize inside and outside account managers to support commercialization 
activities. Contractor will: 
• Review pending IRU Agreements and negotiate with potential Users. 
• Identify potential Users via 
▪ Existing relationships 
▪ New business development activities 
▪ Conferences and trade events 
▪ Other forms of advertising 
• Contact potential Users via phone, email, social media and face-to-face meetings to 
generate interest and drive sales. 
 
Intermediary Services. 
Contractor will provide intermediary services during contract discussions with Users. After all 
negotiations are complete and final changes have been made to the User Agreement terms and

acceptance. During this process, Contractor will:

SCHEDULE 5.4 
 
PROPOSED DESIGN PLANS; AS-BUILT DESIGN PLANS 
 
Segment 1 of the network originates at an access point near the APS Cholla Power Plant and 
runs east along I-40 to Holbrook and terminates at an access point near the Summit 
Healthcare Clinic.   
 
Segment 2 runs from the Summit Healthcare Clinic and turns south along Highway 77 
towards Snowflake and Taylor where it will terminate at an access point near the Snowflake 
Taylor Police Department.   
 
Segment 3 runs from Snowflake passing through Taylor and Shumway along Highway 77.  
The network will continue west and southwest on Lone Pine Dam Rd. approximately seven 
(7) miles north of Show Low to avoid a largely Basalt rock plateau.  From Lone Pine Dam 
Rd., the network will continue south to Highway 260 and back into Show Low from the west 
side along old Linden Rd. and Deuce of Clubs Ave. where it will terminate in an access point 
near the intersection with Highway 260.   
 
Segment 4 runs from Show Low and will continue south on Highway 260 through Lakeside 
and to Pinetop where it will terminate in an access point near the Summit Health Pinetop 
Medical facility.   
 
Segment 5 runs from Pinetop along Highway 260 where it terminates near the Fort Apache 
Indian reservation border. 
 
The secondary backbone route of the network is comprised of one segment which consists of 
approximately 156,000 ft. of 288-count single mode fiber installed 100% underground in a 
new 1.25” duct with a second spare 1.25” duct running from Show Low to Heber-Overgaard.   
 
Segment 6 originates at Highway 260 and the intersection with the Lone Pine Dam Rd. 
segment from the primary backbone.  The segment heads west on Highway 260  to Heber-
Overgaard where it will terminate at an access point near the intersection of Highway 260 
and Highway 277.

SCHEDULE 7.1 
 
FIBER OPTIC SYSTEM MAINTENANCE 
 
1. MAINTENANCE OF THE FIBER AND CONDUIT 
 
(a) Scheduled Maintenance. Routine maintenance and repair of conduit and fiber ("Scheduled 
Maintenance") shall include the following activities: 
 
(i) Patrol of the System Route on a regularly scheduled basis,  
 
(ii) Maintenance of a “Call -Before-You-Dig” program, where applicable, a nd all 
required and related cable locates; and 
 
(iii) Maintenance of signposts along the System Route with a phone number; and 
 
(iv) Assignment of fiber maintenance employees to locations along the System Route 
at reasonable intervals dependent upon terrain, accessibility, locate ticket volume, 
etc. 
 
(b) Unscheduled Maintenance. Non-routine maintenance and repair of the fibers and conduit, 
which is not included as Scheduled Maintenance, shall be performed by or under the 
direction of Contractor (“Unscheduled Maintenance”).   
 
Unscheduled Maintenance shall include response to an alarm identification by Contractor’s 
TSC or County’s Operations Center with notification to Contractor by County or 
notification to Contractor by any third party of any fail ure, interruption or impairment in 
the operation of the fibers or conduit, or any event imminently likely to cause the failure, 
interruption or impairment in the operation of the fibers or conduit. 
 
County shall report the need for Unscheduled Maintenance to Contractor in accordance 
with procedures promulgated by Contractor from time to time. Contractor will log the time 
of County’s report, verify the problem and dispatch personnel to take corrective action. 
 
If Unscheduled Maintenance is required, the Cont ractor shall charge the following time 
and materials rates in connection with the performance of Unscheduled Maintenance.   
Costs of any Unscheduled Maintenance shall be allocated to County pro rata based on the 
number of County Fibers and the total fiber count in the affected portion of the System. 
 
Description Unit Rate 
Project Manager Hour $161.70 
Engineering Manager Hour $158.55 
Maintenance Manager Hour $132.30

The time and materials rates shall be increased on each anniversary of the System 
Acceptance Date by the increase, if any, in the CPI for the preceding twelve (12) month 
period.  In the event such index shall cease to be  computed or published, Contractor may, 
in its reasonable discretion, designate a successor index to be used in determining any 
increase to the Maintenance Fee 
 
2. COOPERATION AND COORDINATION. 
 
(a) County shall utilize an escalation list, as updated from time to time, to report and seek 
immediate action on exceptions noted in the performance of Contractor in meeting the 
maintenance service objectives. 
 
(b) In performing its services hereunder, Contractor shall take workmanlike care to prevent 
impairment to the signal continuity and performance of the fibers.  The precautions to be 
taken by Contractor shall include notifications to County.  In addition, Contractor shall 
reasonably cooperate with County in sharing information and analyzing the disturbances 
regarding the fibers. In the event that any Scheduled or Unscheduled Maintenance 
hereunder requires a traffic roll or reconfiguration involving fibers, electronic equipment, 
or regeneration or other facilities of County, then County shall, at Contractor’s reasonable 
request, make such personnel of County available as may be necessary in order to 
accomplish such maintenance, which personnel shall coordinate and cooperate with 
Contractor in performing such maintenance as required of County hereunder. 
 
3. MAINTENANCE WINDOW.  
 
Scheduled Maintenance, which is reasonably expected to produce any signal discontinuity, 
must be coordinated between the parties. Contractor shall use commercially reasonable 
efforts to pro vide County five ( 5) days advance notice of Scheduled M aintenance.  
Generally, this work should be scheduled after midnight and before 6:00 a.m. local time 
and on certain weekends (“Maintenance Window”). 
 
4. RESTORATION OF THE FIBERS. 
 
(a) Contractor shall maintain sufficient capability to teleconference with County during an 
Unscheduled Maintenance event in order to provide regular communications during the 
restoration process.  When correcting or repairing fiber optic cable discontinuity or 
damage, including but not limited to, an event of Unscheduled Maintenance, Contractor 
shall use reasonable efforts to repair traffic -affecting discontinuity within eight (8) hours 
after the Contractor’s maintenance employee’s arrival at the problem site.  In order to 
accomplish such objective, it is acknowledged that the repairs so effected may be

<!-- page 626 -->
-3- 
temporary in nature.  In such event, within twenty-four (24) hours after completion of any 
such Unscheduled Maintenance, Contractor shall commence its planning for permanent 
repair, and thereafter promptly shall notify County of such plans, and shall implement such 
permanent repair within an appropriate time thereafter. Restoration of open fibers on fiber 
strands not immediately required for service shall be completed on a mutually agreed-upon 
schedule.  If the fiber is required for immediate services, the permanent restoration shall 
be scheduled for the next available Maintenance Window.   
 
(b) During restoration, the parties agree to work together to restore all traffic as quic kly as 
possible. Contractor, promptly upon arriving on the site of the cut, shall determine the 
course of action to be taken to restore the fibers and shall begin restoration efforts. 
Contractor shall splice fibers in accordance with affected systems, as jointly agreed upon.  
 
(c) In performing permanent repairs, Contractor shall comply with industry standard splicing 
specifications, as defined in Schedule 2.1, Scope of Work.   
 
(d) Contractor’s representatives that are responsible for initial restoration of a cut fiber optic 
cable shall carry on their vehicles the typical appropriate equipment that would enable a 
temporary splice, if deemed to be necessary. However , Contractor  will evaluate each 
situation and determine the timeliest and most cost-effective manner of restoration, with 
the prime objective being restoration of operating capability. 
 
(e) County shall provide to Contractor the class of laser light and optical density being emitted 
from the County's equipment. 
 
5.  MOVES, ADDS AND CHANGES 
 
  Design and Construction Services. Should the Parties agree that System modifications are 
required, then a Task Order for Design and Construction Services may be entered into by 
the Parties pursuant to Section 5.7 of this Contract.    
 
  Lateral Segments.  The System may be comprised of certain lateral extensions of the duct 
and fiber optic cable (“Lateral Segments”) that are constructed from the backbone of the 
System to a separate connection point (e.g., manhole).  Contractor will charge the time and 
material rates noted above to the County or those System Users who requested such Lateral 
Segments.  Should the County install additional backbone duct or fiber optic facilities that 
increases the mileage of the System by more than one (1) mile in aggregate, the Contractor 
shall be entitled to an increase in the Scheduled Maintenance Fee. 
   
  Utility Relocations and Cooperation with Others.  Contractor is responsible for verifying 
the nature and status of all utility relocation work and for taking ap propriate measures to 
ensure that Contractor's construction operations do not interfere with utility facilities and 
relocation work.    County shall be responsible for locating or marking all County 
underground utilities with the exception of the fiber opt ic conduit and cable System.  
Contractor shall be responsible for confirming the exact locations of all utilities and to 
safely schedule and coordinate utility relocations, if any.

ARTICLE 7. 
ACCEPTANCE TESTING AND COMPLETION 
 
7.01 Grantor shall test the Grantee Fibers in accordance with the procedures and standards specified 
in Exhibit D ("Acceptance Testing") and Grantor shall provide Grantee with a copy of such test results so 
that the test results may be reviewed in a timely manner.  Acceptance Testing is limited to testing of the 
Grantee Fibers.  Grantee shall be responsible for the t imely designation of its space and power 
requirements and completion of any work or installation required in order for it to place the Grantee Fibers 
into operation (and Grantee's failure to designate its space and power requirements or complete such work 
shall not be grounds for rejection of a Completion Notice). 
 
7.02 Upon the successful completion of Acceptance Testing for each Segment, Grantor shall provide 
written notice of same to Grantee (a "Completion Notice").  Grantor shall contemporaneously deliver a copy 
of the results of the Acceptance Testing (if and to the extent that Grantor has not previously delivered same) 
and Grantee shall, within fifteen (15) days of receipt of the Completion Notice, either accept or reject the 
Completion Notice (Grantee  shall be permitted to reject only if Grantee specifies a material failure of the 
Grantee Fibers to satisfy the requirements of this Agreement) by delivery of written notice to Grantor.  In 
the event Grantee rejects the Completion Notice, Grantor shall pro mptly, and at no cost of Grantee, 
commence to remedy the defect or failure specified in Grantee's notice. Thereafter Grantor shall again 
conduct Acceptance Testing for that Segment and (if successfully completed) provide Grantee a new 
Completion Notice.  T he foregoing procedure shall apply again and succes sively thereafter until Grantor 
has remedied all defects or failures specified by Grantee.  Any failure by Grantee to timely accept or reject 
a Completion Notice, or any use of the Grantee Fibers by Grantee for any purpose other than testing of the 
Grantee Fibers, shall be deemed to constitute acceptance for purposes of this Agreement and Grantee 
shall be deemed to have delivered a notice of acceptance upon such use or on the fifteenth (15th) day after 
delivery of the Completion Notice.

Exhibit "C" 
Fiber Specifications 
 
1.  The fiber optic cable shall be single armor in design. The cable may be either loose tube or central 
core in construction. The central strength member shall be dielectric. Each buffer tube or ribbon 
shall contain 12 fibers. 
 
2.  The glass within the fiber optic cable shall be either Standard Single-Mode or Non-Zero Dispersion-
Shifted, maximized for operation in the broadest wavelength ranges. 
 
3.  All connectors shall be Ultra polished SC-SC unless both Parties agree to another type.

<!-- page 652 -->
1 
Exhibit "D" 
Acceptance Testing Procedures and Standards 
 
1. All splices will be performed with an industry-accepted fusion splicing machine. 
 
2. Splices will be qualified during initial construction with an Optical Time Domain Reflectometer 
(OTDR) from only one direction. The profile alignment system or light injection detection system on 
the fusion splicer may be used to qualify splices in lieu of an OTDR, provided both Parties agree a 
close correlation to the OTDR values can be established.  
 
3. Bi-directional span testing will be done from fiber termination panel to fiber termination panel.  
 
3.1 Installed loss measurements at 1550 nm will be recorded using an industry -accepted laser 
source. 
 
3.2 OTDR traces will be taken at 1550 rim and splice loss measurements will be analyzed. GN 
Nettest Laser Precision or EXFO format will be used on all traces, unless another OTDR 
format is agreed to by both Parties. Launch reels will not be used for the span OTDR traces. 
 
3.3 All testing will be conducted at 1550 nm only. 
 
3.4 OTDR traces shall be saved in a standard file naming convention. 
 
3.5 One set of diskettes with all traces will be submitted. 
 
4. The splicing standards are as follows: 
 
4.1 The objective loss value of the connector and its associated splice will be 0.50 dB or less. 
This value does not include the insertion loss from its connection to the FDP.  
 
4.2 The objective for each fiber within a span shall be an average bi -directional loss of 0.10dB  
or less for each splice. For example, if a given span has 10 splices, each fiber shall have a 
total bi-directional loss (due to the 10 splices) of 1.0 dB or less. Individual bi -directional loss 
values for each splice will be reviewed for high losses, which may indicate splice instability. 
 
4.3 The aforementioned standards are objectives, not the basis for acceptance. The acceptance 
standard for each fiber shall be an average bi-directional installed loss of 0.30 dB/km or less 
across each span. 
 
5. All connector splices will be protected with heat shrinks. Backbone splices may be stored in trays 
with bare fiber manifolds and RTV silicone protection.  In no cases will more than 24 fibers be stored 
in any single tray.  Buffer tubes/ribbons will not be split across more than one splice tray. An industry-
accepted non-encapsulated splice enclosure will be used on all splices (like PLP Coyote, Lucent 
2600, or 3M 2178). 
 
6. The entire fiber optic cable system shall be properly protected from foreign voltage and grounded 
with an industry-accepted system. 
 
7. Connectors shall be Ultra polished SC with conventional single mode glass.

Maintenance Requirements and Procedures 
 
1. MAINTENANCE OF THE FIBER AND CONDUIT 
 
(a) Scheduled Maintenance. Routine maintenance and repair of conduit and fiber shall include 
the following activities: 
 
(i) Patrol of the System Route on a regularly scheduled basis,  
 
(ii) Maintenance of a “Call -Before-You-Dig” program, where applicable, and all 
required and related cable locates; and 
 
(iii) Maintenance of signposts along the System Route with a phone number; and 
 
(iv) Assignment of fiber maintenance employees to locations along the System Route  
at reasonable intervals dependent upon terrain, accessibility, locate ticket 
volume, etc. 
 
(b) Unscheduled Maintenance. Non-routine maintenance and repair of the fibers and conduit, 
which is not included as Scheduled Maintenance, shall be performed by or under the 
direction of Grantor (“Unscheduled Maintenance”).   
 
Unscheduled Maintenance shall include response to an ala rm identification by Grantor’s 
TSC or Grantee’s Operations Center with notification to Grantor, notification to Grantor by 
Grantee or notification to Grantor by any third party of any failure, interruption or impairment 
in the operation of the fibers or conduit, or any event imminently likely to cause the failure, 
interruption or impairment in the operation of the fibers or conduit. 
 
Grantee shall report the need for Unscheduled Maintenance to Grantor in accordance with 
procedures promulgated by Grantor from time to time. Grantor will log the time of Grantee’s 
report, verify the problem and dispatch personnel to take corrective action.  
 
If Unscheduled Maintenance is required, the Grantor shall charge the following time and 
materials rates in connection with the performance of Unscheduled Maintenance.   Costs 
of any Unscheduled Maintenance shall be allocated to Grantee pro rata based on the 
number of Grantee Fibers and the total fiber count in the affected portion of the Grantor 
System.

2. COOPERATION AND COORDINATION. 
 
(a) Grantee shall utilize an escalation list, as updated from time to time, to report and seek 
immediate action on exceptions noted in the performance of Grantor in meeting the 
maintenance service objectives. 
 
(b) In performing its services hereunder, Grantor shall take workmanlike care to prevent 
impairment to the signal continuity and perform ance of the fibers.  The precautions to be 
taken by Grantor shall include notifications to Grantee.  In addition, Grantor shall 
reasonably cooperate with Grantee in sharing information and analyzing the disturbances 
regarding the Grantee Fibers. In the eve nt that any Scheduled or Unscheduled 
Maintenance hereunder requires a traffic roll or reconfiguration involving fibers, electronic 
equipment, or regeneration or other facilities of Grantee, then Grantee shall, at Grantor’s 
reasonable request, make such per sonnel of Grantee available as may be necessary in 
order to accomplish such maintenance, which personnel shall coordinate and cooperate 
with Grantor in performing such maintenance as required of Grantee hereunder.  
 
3. MAINTENANCE WINDOW.  
 
Scheduled Maintenance, which is reasonably expected to produce any signal discontinuity, 
must be coordinated between the Parties. Grantor shall use commercially reasonable 
efforts to provide Grantee 5 days advance notice of scheduled maintenance.  Generally, 
this work should be scheduled after midnight and before 6:00 a.m. local time and on certain 
weekends (“Maintenance Window”). 
 
 
4. RESTORATION OF THE FIBERS. 
 
(a) Grantor shall maintain sufficient capability to teleconference with Grantee during an 
Unscheduled Maintenan ce in order to provide regular communications during the 
restoration process.  When correcting or repairing fiber optic cable discontinuity or damage, 
including but not limited to, an event of Unscheduled Maintenance, Grantor shall use 
reasonable efforts t o repair traffic -affecting discontinuity within eight (8) hours after the 
Grantor’s maintenance employee’s arrival at the problem site.  In order to accomplish such 
objective, it is acknowledged that the repairs so effected may be temporary in nature.  In 
such event, within twenty -four (24) hours after completion of any such Unscheduled 
Maintenance, Grantor shall commence its planning for permanent repair, and thereafter 
promptly shall notify Grantee of such plans, and shall implement such permanent repair 
within an appropriate time thereafter. Restoration of open fibers on fiber strands not 
immediately required for service shall be completed on a mutually agreed -upon schedule.  
If the fiber is required for immediate services, the permanent restoration shall be scheduled 
for the next available Maintenance Window.   
 
(b) During restoration, the parties agree to work together to restore all traffic as quickly as 
possible. Grantor, promptly upon arriving on the site of the cut, shall determine the course 
of action to be taken to restore the fibers and shall begin restoration efforts. Grantor shall 
splice fibers in accordance with affected systems, as jointly agreed upon.  
 
(c) In performing permanent repairs, Grantor shall comply with industry standard splicing 
specifications, as defined in Exhibit D.   
 
(d) Grantor’s representatives that are responsible for initial restoration of a cut fiber optic cable 
shall carry on their vehicles the typical appropriate equipment that would enable a 
temporary splice, if deemed to be necessary. However, Grantor will evaluate each situation 
and determine the timeliest and most cost -effective manner of restoration, with the prime 
objective being restoration of operating capability.

Board of Supervisors Regular 7. a.        
Meeting Date: 02/28/2023  
Title: Participation in Opioid Settlement with Teva, Allegran, CVS, Walgreens, Wal-Mart
Submitted For: Jason Moore, Deputy County Attorney 
Submitted By: Jason Moore, Deputy County Attorney
Department: County Attorney
Presented By: Jason Moore
Motion before the Board:
Consideration and possible approval of Navajo County's participation in the settlement
agreement reached in the multi-state opioid litigation case with Teva, Allegan, CVS, Walgreens
and Wal-Mart. 
Background:
Navajo County has been a party to the multi-state opioid litigation for several years now. The
Board of Supervisors has already approved a settlement involving many of the distributors. This
settlement compliments the one already approved by the Board.
Under the terms of their proposed settlements, the companies will pay the following amounts:
Teva to pay up to $4.25 billion, including $3.7 billion to be paid out over 13 years as well as the
option of $1.2 billion worth of its generic version of the drug Narcan over 10 years or an agreed
upon cash equivalent over 13 years;
Allergan to pay up to $2.37 billion over 7 years;
CVS to pay up to $5 billion over 10 years;
Walgreens to pay up to $5.7 billion over 15 years; and
Walmart to pay up to $2.75 billion over 6 years.
Recommendation: 
Recommend that the Board approve the participation Agreement on behalf of Navajo County
and authorize Jason Moore to sign on behalf of the County.

Re:  Five New National Opioid Settlements 
Dear County, City, and Town Leaders: 
Last year, every county , city and town signed on to the One Arizona Distribution of Opioid 
Settlement Funds Agreement, agreeing to the allocation of funds that will be received as a result 
of national opioid settlements.  This agreement provides that the local governments that sign on to 
a settlement receive 56% of the funds distributed to Arizona  from that settlement, 44% going 
to the State. 
 
Your participation helped Arizona maximize the benefits to be received from the first two major 
global settlements.  The first was with three opioid distributors: McKesson, AmerisourceBergen, 
and Cardinal.  The second was with opioid manufacturer Ja nssen/Johnson & Johnson.  These 
settlements will bring up to $549 million into Arizona for opioid treatment, prevention, and 
education.  As you know, payments to Arizona cities, towns and counties from these settlements 
began last year. 
 
Recently, you received communications from Rubris  Inc., the Implementation Administrator, 
announcing five new proposed national opioid settlements.  Arizona has formally indicated its 
conditional approval of these settlements, which  will bring up to an additional $434 million into 
Arizona to address the opioid crisis (see chart).

The process for achieving final approval of these settlements is similar to the process for the earlier

receive funds from them.  The total amount of money Arizonans will receive is dependent on the

number of local governments that sign on, which means you play a vital role in maximizing the 
benefit Arizona can achieve.  Also, only if sufficient subdivisions participate across the nation will 
these settlements be finalized.   
 
In the next few weeks, you will receive another email communication from Rubris with specific 
instructions regarding how to sign on to the agreements and indicate your willingness to participate 
in the settlements.  We ask that every one of you respond as soon as possible, but no later than the 
deadline of April 18, 2023. 
 
Remember, you must sign on to each agreement in order to share in the settlement funds from that 
settlement.  If you do not sign on to an agreement, you are not eligible to receive funds from that 
settlement.  To sign on, you must follow the instructions provided by Rubris.   
 
You may participate in the settlements whether or not you filed a lawsuit or are represented by 
counsel.  However, if you are represented by an attorney with respect to opioid claims, be sure to 
contact them to ensure that everyone is fully informed.  Settlement terms for each agreement may 
be found at https://nationalopioidsettlement.com
.  A copy of the One Arizona Distribution of 
Opioid Settlement Funds Agreement may be found there as well.  Feel free to reach out to Leslie 
Cooper, Division Chief, at Leslie.Cooper@azag.gov or Jane Fallon, Assistant Attorney General, 
at Jane.Fallon@azag.gov with questions or concerns. 
 
Please join me in the fight against the opioids epidemic in Arizona by timely submitting your 
subdivision sign on so we can maximize the funds Arizona will receive from the five new national 
opioid settlements.

Title: Purchase of a 2022 CV515 SFA (3 Yard Dump Truck)
Submitted For: Madhav Mundle, Public Works Director

Department: Public Works

Motion before the Board:
Consideration of the purchase of a 2022 CV515 SFA (3 Yard Dump Truck) from RWC
Group in the amount of $127,332.00.
Background:
The 3 Yard Dump Truck is a replacement for a truck the Heber Road Yard used to have, which,
due to daily wear and tear, and continued mechanical issues and breakage, was budgeted to be
replaced this fiscal year.  This truck is utilized for numerous maintenance activities such as
patching, chip sealing, snow plowing, and cracksealing.
The State of Arizona has a contract with RWC Group (Contract No. CTR041813) for the
purchase of Medium and Heavy Duty Cabs, Chasis, and Buses and this contract is available
for cooperative use.  The price under this contract is fair and reasonable.
 
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends approval of the purchase of a 2022 CV515 SFA (3 Yard Dump Truck)
from RWC Group for the amount of $127,332.00.

Motion before the Board:
PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration and adoption of Resolution Number 04-2023,
approving/denying text amendment to Article 25 of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance
regarding the prohibition against placement/movement of mobile homes 20 years old or older. 
Background:
The Arizona Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) requires all mobile homes
of a jurisdiction-indicated age to be certified as rehabilitated in accordance with current
HUD-established safety standards, in accordance with R4-34-606. The Navajo County Zoning
Ordinance currently reflects the HUD-indicated age at which mobile homes must obtain
certification of rehabilitation as having been prior to June 15, 1976. Navajo County updated to
the 2018 IRC/IBC on June 22, 2022 to reflect modern safety standards. As a result, the
proposed Zoning Ordinance Text Amendment attempts to bridge the gap between 1976
standards and 2018 standards for mobile home safety assurance upon relocation of older
dwellings.
Recommendation: 
Planning and Development Staff and the Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission
recommend the text amendment to Article 25 of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance.

NAVAJO COUNTY 
 
PLANNING AND DEVELOPMENT 
 
 
BOARD OF SUPERVISORS 
 
 
STAFF REPORT  
 
TO:  Board of Supervisors 
 
FROM:  Sondra Starke, Planner I 
  
HEARING DATE:  February 28, 2023   
 
PROJECT NUMBER:  TXT-A 23 -002 AMENDMENTS TO ARTICLE 25 – 
PROHIBITION AGAINST  PLACEMENT/MOVEMENT OF  
MOBILE HOMES 20 YEARS OLD OR OLDER:  Consideration 
of text amendment to Article 25, Section 2517 of the Navajo County 
Zoning Ordinance, regarding age of mobile home which requires 
HUD rehabilitation certification. 
 
 
BACKGROUND 
 
The Arizona Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) requires all mobile homes of 
a jurisdiction -indicated age to be certified as rehabilitated in accordance  with current HUD-
established safety standards, in accordance with R4-34-606. The Navajo County Zoning Ordinance 
currently reflects the HUD-indicated age at which mobile homes must obtain certification of 
rehabilitation as having been prior to June 15, 1976 . Navajo County updated to the 2018 IRC/IBC 
on June 22, 2022 to reflect modern safety standards. As a result, the proposed Zoning Ordinance 
Text Amendment attempts to bridge the gap between 1976 standards and 2018 standards for mobile 
home safety assurance upon relocation of older dwellings.  
 
STAFF ANALYSIS 
 
The efforts put forth by Navajo County to promote safety and wellness within the community by 
adopting the 2018 IRC and 2018 IBC have clarified that all development in the community shall be 
held to a regulated and modern standard of quality. In effect, mobile home movement must also be 
done in a regulated manner to ensure that Navajo County is a safe county in which to reside. Navajo 
County has discovered a discrepancy within which mobile homes manufac tured between June of 
1976 and the current day that would benefit from HUD certification to verify safe living standards 
and assist homeowners in rehabilitation awareness  are being relocated in their uncertified state s.

<!-- page 674 -->
Board of Supervisors                                      February 28, 2023        2 | P a g e  
This gap in coverage provides for unsafe homes to remain unsafe, whereas updating the requirement 
to a rolling 20 -year basis would provide for an opportunity to ensure that the mobile homes to be 
relocated are safe and habitable by modern standards. 
  
Staff has determined through research that, by continuing to follow the HUD-indicated age marker 
of June 22, 1976, there is a considerable concern with the above discrepancy, which validates interest 
in adjusting the age threshold by a minimum of 20 years on a rolling basis. While researching, Staff 
findings included a section of the Rehabilitation Assistance Packet on the State of Arizona 
Department of Housing website that gives notice to applicants that the local jurisdiction may have 
age requirements that exceed the threshold determined by HUD: 
 
“Please verify the local zoning requirements with the city, town or county BEFORE 
planning to relocate a mobile home. Some local jurisdictions have requirements that 
exceed the state requirements; some local jurisdictions do not allow mobile homes.” 
  
Additionally, Staff found that there is a financial assistance program through the HUD Relocation 
Fund which can reimburse rehabilitation costs  up to $1,500.00 to the homeowner if they are at , or 
below, the current federal poverty guideline set by the Unit ed States Department of Health and 
Human Services. Information for this program is available on the HUD website . Fees for 
rehabilitation certification are dependent on income in that there is a discounted rate for homeowners 
under the federal poverty guideline. 
 
Based upon the above, Staff is currently recommending that the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance 
be updated to require all mobile homes 20 years old or older to be HUD rehabilitation certified and 
permitted by Navajo County prior to relocation. At the Thursday, January 19th Planning and Zoning 
Commission hearing, the Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission unanimously 
recommended approval of this proposed text amendment.  
 
Within the attachments of this Staff report, the Board of Supervisors will find a track changes and 
clean copy version of the amendments, as currently proposed by Staff.

Section 2517 – Prohibition Against Placement/Movement of Mobile Homes Built Before June 15, 
1976 20 Years Old or Older 
 
Notwithstanding any other provision of the Zoning Ordinance, from and after January 1, 2000 April 
1, 2023, no Mobile Home as defined in A.R.S. §41-2142 (i.e., a structure built prior to June 15, 1976, 
on a permanent chassis, capable of being transported in  one or more sections and designed to be 
used with or without a permanent foundation as a dwelling when connected to on-site utilities, except 
a Recreational Vehicle or Factory-Built Building) 20 years old or older at the time of application for 
mobile home, manufactured home permit shall be located within the unincorporated area of Navajo

of Navajo County.    This prohibition shall likewise not apply to any Mobile Home that has been

owner shall obtain cause the Mobile Home to be certified as rehabilitated to HUD standards prior to

SECTION 2. Severability. 
 
If any section, subsection, sentence, clause, phrase or por tion of this ordinance or any part 
of the code adopted herein by reference is for any reason held to be invalid or 
unconstitutional by the decision of any court of competent ju risdiction, such decision shall 
not affect the validity of the remaining portions thereof. 
 
SECTION 3. Clerical Corrections 
 
The County Clerk is hereby authorized to correct typographical and grammatical errors, as 
well as errors of wording and punctuation , as necessary related to this ordinance as 
amended herein, and to make formatti ng changes needed for purposes of clarity and form, 
or consistency, within thirty (30) days following adoption by the Board of Supervisors. 
 
SECTION 4. Effective Date 
 
This ordinance shall become effective thirty (30) days following adoption by the Board of 
Supervisors.

PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration of the adoption of Resolution Number 05-2023 
approving/denying a text amendment to Article IX, Navajo County Subdivision Regulations and
Addition of Section 9.4 - Exceptions; Plat Alterations.
Background:
Throughout Navajo County, there are several old subdivisions that were platted before 1969
with CC&R’s stating subdividing is allowed if zoning is met.  So many properties in
subdivisions are already split, without going under the minimum lot size allowed in subject
zoning.  This practice was common and very easy to do by just recording the split with the
County Recorder’s Office.  Navajo County adopted the MLD (Minor Land Division) process in
2018 and these split requests came to Planning staff for review and were rejected in the already
final platted subdivisions.
There were complaints made by property owners that it had been done by their neighbors in the
past, or there were already so many splits in the subdivision, or they bought their property with
the intention of splitting because their CC&Rs indicated that they could split their properties.
Staff formed an ad-hoc task force to explore the problem in depth. After several months of
work, the staff findings were: 
Some Arizona counties already do the lot-split process in existing, old, platted
subdivisions,
The Navajo County has evaluated this for a long time and feels there are conditions under
which such splits would be acceptable,
The staff held a work session with the P&Z Commission in April 2022 where this issue
was discussed.  After hearing the staff’s overview of the issues and hearing from two
different property owners who were dealing with the issue, there was consensus of the
commission for staff to find a solution. (See minutes in attachments).
The Planning and Zoning Commission heard this item at their January 19, 2023, meeting and
recommended approval to the Board of Supervisors by a 7-0 vote.

amendment and addition of Section 9.4 to Article IX.  
 
 
The Navajo County Subdivision Ordinance was adopted in January 1969  and has not been 
amended or revised since 2007.   
 
BACKGROUND:   
Throughout the Navajo County, there are several old subdivisions that are platted before 1969 
with CC&R’s stat ing subdividing is allowed if zoning is met.   So many properties in 
subdivisions are already split, without going under the minimum lot size allowed in subject 
zoning.  This practice was common and very easy to do by just recording the split with the 
County Recorder’ s Office.  Navajo County adopted MLD (Minor Land Division) process in 
2018 and these splits  requests were coming to Planning staff for review and were getting 
rejected in already final platted subdivisions.  
 
There were complaints by the property owner that the neighbor has done it, or there are already 
so many of the splits in the subdivision, or they bought  their property with the intention of 
splitting because their CC&Rs indicated that they could split.   
 
Staff formed an ad -hoc task force to explore the problem in depth. After several months of 
work, staff findings were: 
 
• Some Arizona counties already do lot split process in existing, old, 
platted subdivisions,

<!-- page 690 -->

• The Navajo County has evaluated this for a long time and feels there are 
conditions under which such splits would be acceptable, 
 
• Staff held a work session with P&Z Commission in April 2022 where 
this issue discussed.  Af ter hearing staff’s overview of the issues and 
hearing from two different property owners who were dealing with the 
issue, there was consensus of the commission for staff to find a solution. 
(See minutes in attachments). 
 
Planning and Development staff alo ng with legal realized wording in 9.4 had some ambiguity 
in it.  The intent is now clearer and did not change from what was presented to and approved by 
the Planning and Zoning Commission. 
 
Resolution is to add a text amendment which allows subdividing within platted subdivisions as 
outlined below: 
 
SECTION 9.4 Exceptions; Plat Alterations 
 
Subdividing property in an approved platted subdivision that adds density is prohibited 
without going through the final plat process described in Article VI of this ordinance.  
However, if one of the conditions specified in paragraph A or B are present, an applicant does 
not have to go through the final plat process described in Article VI, as long as the subject 
property meets the requirements contained in paragraph C of this section. 
 
A. The subdivision has Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions (CC&Rs) 
recorded with the Navajo County Recorder’s office in 1973 or earlier   
that stipulate that the subdividing of lots was envisioned at the time the 
final subdivision plat was approved.  Approval of proposed subdividing 
of a lot shall be considered within the criteria enumerated in this section, 
regardless of the conditions, stipulations or allowances in said CC&Rs. 
 
B. The subdivision was platted and approved by the Board of Supervisors 
in 1970 or earlier.  A list of subdivisions meeting conditions  A. and B. 
shall be maintained by Navajo County. 
 
C. A subdivided lot as considered in this section shall be: a minimum of one 
acre; shall provide frontage of one-hundred feet on a publicly dedicated 
and accepted street or a private road approved and accepted by the 
County and which has been established by a plat, recorded subdivision 
or otherwise established by some legal instrument of record which is 
described and denot ed as such. The deputy public works director for 
planning and development services may exercise limited discretion for 
these requirements as set forth in Section 2509 - Administrative Waiver 
of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance.
